6CchqJ.description: Limited Production To learn about the performance characteristics of specific glasses, visit About Our Glass . For details about sheet glass sizes, visit What to Expect from Bullseye Glass

3F8eWM.name: Mixed Opalescent Colors
3F8eWM.description: Stringer Threads of glass pulled from re-melted Bullseye Compatible sheet. For use in kilnforming or torchworking. Stringers come in 0.5 mm (“Fine Line”), 1 mm, and 2 mm thicknesses and are approximately 17.75" (451 mm) long. They are packed in clear plastic tubes that are 18" (457 mm) long and 0.75" (19 mm) in diameter. Tubes are packaged by volume. A tube of .0.5 mm stringer contains approximately 350 pieces. A tube of 1 mm stringers contains approximately 123 pieces. A tube of 2 mm stringer contains approximately 50 pieces. Tubes of colors made with gold contain fewer stringers, to reduce unit price. For example, a tube of gold-bearing 1 mm stringers contains approximately 87 pieces, while a tube of 2 mm stringers contains approximately 33 pieces. Like our sheet glass, stringers are made by hand. There may be slight variation in color, thickness, length, etc.

2hC9hK.name: Mixed Transparent Colors
2hC9hK.description: Stringer Threads of glass pulled from re-melted Bullseye Compatible sheet. For use in kilnforming or torchworking. Stringers come in 0.5 mm (“Fine Line”), 1 mm, and 2 mm thicknesses and are approximately 17.75" (451 mm) long. They are packed in clear plastic tubes that are 18" (457 mm) long and 0.75" (19 mm) in diameter. Tubes are packaged by volume. A tube of .0.5 mm stringer contains approximately 350 pieces. A tube of 1 mm stringers contains approximately 123 pieces. A tube of 2 mm stringer contains approximately 50 pieces. Tubes of colors made with gold contain fewer stringers, to reduce unit price. For example, a tube of gold-bearing 1 mm stringers contains approximately 87 pieces, while a tube of 2 mm stringers contains approximately 33 pieces. Like our sheet glass, stringers are made by hand. There may be slight variation in color, thickness, length, etc.

3fPm9a.name: Opaline Opalescent
3fPm9a.description: The unique mix in this style will create a strong reaction and not reveal (or strike to) its target color until fired. Limited Production To learn about the performance characteristics of specific glasses, visit About Our Glass . For details about sheet glass sizes, visit What to Expect from Bullseye Glass

5tut62.name: Indigo Blue Opalescent
5tut62.description: Limited Production To learn about the performance characteristics of specific glasses, visit About Our Glass . For details about sheet glass sizes, visit What to Expect from Bullseye Glass

5UsgHZ.name: White Opalescent
5UsgHZ.description: Limited Production To learn about the performance characteristics of specific glasses, visit About Our Glass . For details about sheet glass sizes, visit What to Expect from Bullseye Glass

1DRaWM.name: White
1DRaWM.description: The unique mix in this style will create a strong reaction and not reveal (or strike to) its target color until fired. Limited Production Windows - Part of the fun and mystery of these styles is that no two are alike. Expect variation! To learn about the performance characteristics of specific glasses, visit About Our Glass . For details about sheet glass sizes, visit What to Expect from Bullseye Glass

6FR3WV.name: Sangre
6FR3WV.description: A dense and saturated bright striking transparent red. Click here to view Sangre Uniques "Sangre has always been my favorite transparent red. Just the right amount of brightness and doesn’t get 'livered' or brownish if you work it for a long time. I made a simple spacer bead. I also made a second bead with a base of Effetre Super Clear. The left side was then encased in Effetre white to represent the opaque, the middle in CiM Marshmallow to represent the translucent, and finally the right remained clear to represent the transparent. Sangre was then wound onto this bead. This gives the opportunity to see encasement in a variety of common beadmaking situations.” – Kim Fields

2jUEcn.name: Maraschino
2jUEcn.description: A dense transparent bright carnival red. "Maraschino does some interesting things when fumed by silvered ivory." – Chris Haussler

3QqGNC.name: Firecracker
3QqGNC.description: An opaque dark cherry red. Hillary Lawson created this gorgeous tutorial featuring CiM Firecracker, Crocus, & Wisteria. Visit Glass Alchemist for the video portion of the tutorial [and other tutorials as well]. – Hillary Lawson

1MAzw4.name: Garnet
1MAzw4.description: A garnet red. "I made a sculptural bird bead with Garnet. I began with a clear 'core' body and encased in Garnet. This gives an opportunity to see encasement. The head, wings and tail were added straight from the rod. I used Reichenbach Deep Black for the base of the beak followed by Effetre Pastel Yellow. The eyes are also Reichenbach Deep Black." – Kim Fields

213YnP.name: Maroon
213YnP.description: A dense maroon red. "The main beads show the base glass with metallic armour created with Double Helix Triton shards. The two glasses were meant to be together like a romance with the silver glass producing shades from gold, pink and blue." Read more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

1Bcqwd.name: Vampire
1Bcqwd.description: A dark, rich opaque red that will not liver. "Rich red with a tad blue tone. I love the striations in the red tones. Smooth and easy to melt. Comparison beads on top right are Effetre medium red [left] and Sangre [right]." – Jean Daniels

30567t.name: Almandine
30567t.description: A dark, rich wine red. Almandine with gold. – Pauline Chevalier

6qzycZ.name: Goji
6qzycZ.description: A goji berry orange-red. "Goji is a super bright orange red. Semi-translucent or almost opaque. Lovely bright shade, sculpts well, and it appears to be a nice stable color." – Anna Miller

1T3QCZ.name: Clockwork
1T3QCZ.description: A vibrant and saturated striking orange that ranges from transparent to translucent to opaque, depending on your working style and atmosphere. Hillary Lawson created this gorgeous tutorial featuring CiM Clockwork. Visit Glass Alchemist for the video portion of the tutorial [and other tutorials as well]. – Hillary Lawson

5qbbN1.name: Phoenix
5qbbN1.description: An opaque that can be struck to a range of hues from peach to orange coral. Check out Claudia Trimbur-Pagel’s Pirate bead tutorial in the January 2013 issue of the Soda Lime Times . – Claudia Trimbur-Pagel

2eYB9f.name: Marigold
2eYB9f.description: An opaque orange. "I tested Marigold as a dot. Often red/yellow/oranges don't do well as dots . . . they can strike and not leave crisp edges. But as you can see Marigold gave great results!" – Trudi Doherty

72ett5.name: Pumpkin Unique 2
72ett5.description: An opaque orange. Left to right: Pumpkin, Pumpkin Unique -1, Pumpkin Unique -2, Pumpkin Unique -3, Pumpkin Unique -4. – Claudia Eidenbenz

6YL6wU.name: Daffodil
6YL6wU.description: An opaque orange. "I find the Effetre yellows to be either vile-looking or not opaque enough but Daffodil is just beautiful. It's a deep, vibrant yellow and again, it works perfectly as stringer and I had no encasing issues. That's right, a yellow that you can encase." Read more at Laura's blog . – Laura Sparling

2JDDm9.name: Alley Cat
2JDDm9.description: An opaque orange. "Alley Cat is such a great orange - very pumpkin. Easy to work with and a staple in my palette." – Bling Squared Cute Glass

36pAzG.name: Orange Crush
36pAzG.description: A bright transparent orange that turns opaque when worked. Crocus over Orange Crush. – Gloria Sevey

66U6KG.name: Butternut
66U6KG.description: An opaque orange. "Butternut - a juicy, squashy orange that lives up to its name absolutely. If you want an earthy or happy orange - this is your colour." Read more at DragonJools blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

0y4TFR.name: Monarch
0y4TFR.description: An opaque yellow orange. "In the pics you can see a bigger bead which base is half Effetre White and half Effetre Dark Ivory. Next there are three basic beads, upper made with reducing flame, middle oxidizing flame and last with neutral flame. Then there is a bead covered deliberately badly with clear, and a black bead with dots over it. Monarch is a well behaving glass. It does not bleed very much, when covered badly with clear glass. . . . You can see in the pic of Monarch, that with hotter Minor flame the dots are not that crispy and they are lighter too. They reacted slightly for the reducing flame, but not too badly. All tested and said, I think that if I need yellow oranges for something, I would gladly use Monarch." Read more at Maikki's blog . – Maija-Leena Autio

0TL6eq.name: Harvest
0TL6eq.description: An opaque earthy orange. "In the pics you can see a bigger bead which base is half Effetre White and half Effetre Dark Ivory. Next there are three basic beads, upper made with reducing flame, middle oxidizing flame and last with neutral flame. Then there is a bead covered deliberately badly with clear, and a black bead with dots over it. Harvest is a well behaving glass. It does not bleed very much, when covered badly with clear glass. I think that if I need yellow oranges for something, I would gladly use Harvest." Read more at Maikki's blog . – Maija-Leena Autio

3tt1Jg.name: Watermelon
3tt1Jg.description: A cloudy transparent orangish red. "Portrait in Watermelon, etched soda-lime glass bead, 2.21" x 1.25" x .79". New CiM Watermelon over a white substrate, Effetre black core. I think the wispy/streaky quality is great for certain designs, but it's not something I prefer. I recommend a cool flame when flamecutting to avoid boiling. Some specs of boiled glass had to be plucked out, but they are manageable." – Laurie Nessel

6TZ4n1.name: Orange-zilla
6TZ4n1.description: A consistent, non-striking intense and juicy orange. Hillary Lawson created this gorgeous tutorial featuring CiM Orange-zilla. Visit Glass Alchemist for the video portion of the tutorial [and other tutorials as well]. – Hillary Lawson

3jNdqm.name: Prometheus
3jNdqm.description: A clear base with reddish orange, orange, and turquoise blue stripes. "Prometheus has ribbons of warm oranges and red encased in transparent clear glass. In my opinion, it’s one of the more exciting streamers. Shown here as spacers, over foil, over Peace, and over Effetre Periwinkle." – Janet Evans

4ML3Tj.name: Solar Storm
4ML3Tj.description: A clear base with reddish orange, orange, and purple stripes. "Solar Storm, I do like it in the flowers." – Dwyn Tomlinson

0MQtrf.name: Sea Anemone
0MQtrf.description: A transparent light purple with reddish orange, yellow, green, and white streamers. "This is Sea Anemone, which appears to be thin strips of orange and red, but when mashed has an overall appearance of pink. That was a surprise! I'm quite pleased with how these turned out!" – Dwyn Tomlinson

4hVywe.name: Marmalade
4hVywe.description: A transparent toasty reddish orange. Hillary Lawson created this gorgeous tutorial featuring CiM Marmalade. Visit Glass Alchemist for the video portion of the tutorial [and other tutorials as well]. – Hillary Lawson

1yKXRY.name: Osage Wood
1yKXRY.description: An apricot orange cloudy transparent. "Nice clean melting, easy to work with and perfect for sculpting. Very nice caramel shade. I must make some glass candy with it." – Anna Miller

2Lk5EL.name: Ocelot
2Lk5EL.description: A clear base with orange, yellow, & black streamers. "I decided to pair Ocelot with a complementary brown glass from my CiM stash - Brown Eyed Girl. This set of tapered barrels used Ocelot as the focal centre stripe with ends of Brown Eyed Girl. I am pleased with how the streamers remained clear and visible with no smearing nor did they disappear or blend together. Both glasses melted smoothly and were a pleasure to work with." Read more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

1XpKGF.name: Cremello Misty
1XpKGF.description: A white misty opal with a hint of peach. "Cremello Misty is a pale opalescent transparent with a hint of peach; easy to work with; not shocky; no bubbling or scum. Did not react with ivory." – Beth Swain

3s5gzs.name: Cremello Milky
3s5gzs.description: A white milky opal with a hint of peach. "Cremello Milky is a pale milky opal glass with a hint of peach; easy to work with; not shocky; no bubbling or scum. Did not react with ivory." – Beth Swain

36XDeU.name: Stone Ground
36XDeU.description: An opaque silver yellow that strikes to a variety of hues. Click here to view Stone Ground Uniques CiM comparison with reduced DH Aurae streams. See more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

3cQTGz.name: Canary
3cQTGz.description: An opaque yellow. "The glass from CiM is wonderfully consistent, and the yellows [including Canary], oranges and red are much more 'what you see is what you get' than the same colour ranges from the Italian manufacturers." Read more at DragonJools blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

4dgUjS.name: Sunny Side Up
4dgUjS.description: An opaque yellow. Formerly Unique Pumpkin -5. "It is a rich, warm colour - and goes a little bit darker and orangey-er than the unworked rod." Read more at DragonJools blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

2w4z75.name: Sunflower
2w4z75.description: An opaque yellow. Formerly Unique Pumpkin -6.

47qV6p.name: Honey Mustard
47qV6p.description: An opaque yellow. "Here, a Honey Mustard base. Left: dotted with CiM Cranberry Pink and CiM Smurfy. Right: dotted with CiM Emperor and CiM Smurfy. Each of the 3 neutral colours 'pool beautifully as small dots over both Cranberry Pink and Emperor." Read more at Kitzbitz Art Glass' blog . – Jolene Wolfe

3jdYJ6.name: Ocher
3jdYJ6.description: An opaque yellow. "A gnome to show support of Ukraine using Ocher. I forgot how much more on the orange side it turns when worked for a long time. It remains my go to color when I work on birds that have a yellow/orange beak, like eagles. A bit too dark to correctly represent the flag color of Ukraine but the spirit is there." – Tammy Mercier

4LeckJ.name: Chamomile
4LeckJ.description: An opaque yellow. "Atypically for CiM- this is a layered glass- which is starting to be a thing that I look for in a glass. Because once you start dragging the glass around, you get much more interesting results, like this." Read more at DragonJools' blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

5TRAn0.name: Yellow Brick Road
5TRAn0.description: An opaque yellow. "Yellow Brick Road is like the Effetre Opal Yellow of old in that you can get it to go different colours depending on the way you treat it. I found that if I made a spacer with Yellow Brick Road, let it round up outside the flame and put it straight in the kiln, I got a lovely even pale lemon yellow. If I gave it a few wafts through the flame after rounding up, its colour darkened slightly, producing a deeper yellow. The intensity of the the yellow also depends on how much of it had been used. Where there is less yellow glass [like in the scroll bead] the yellow is paler, whereas in the spacers and the raised flower, it has a much deeper hue. I noticed that when encased [like the petals of the flower] Yellow Brick Road tends to go much darker and take on an almost pale apricot tinge." Read more at Laura's tumblr . – Laura Sparling

3Fdhqz.name: Painted Hills
3Fdhqz.description: An opaque yellow. "You may have noticed that Stone Ground is a bit thin on the ground right now at the distributors, and you might be wondering what is your best bet as an alternate, and how they stack up. In which case, you might want to have a look at CiM Painted Hills. On the face of it, Painted Hills appears to be much too light to function as an equivalent, but it may actually be closer to Opal Yellow than you think. Here is the bead, still hot, before mashing. From the left, Opal Yellow, Stone Ground, Painted Hills. The dots are Double Helix Aurae." Read more at DragonJools blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

5SNemr.name: Baked Alaska
5SNemr.description: An opaque creamy & reactive yellow. A comparison of Banana Cream, Baked Alaska, & Ra. – Suzy Hannabuss

1HFyK0.name: Scotch Broom
1HFyK0.description: A luminous golden yellow with varying degrees of transparency/opalescence. “If anyone is looking for Ukrainian flag colors, the closest I've come is French Blue encased in dark aqua next to Scotch Broom.” – Hillary Lawson

4Pn541.name: Beeswax Misty
4Pn541.description: A soft pale misty opal yellow that can strike to a deeper amber depending on the time and temperature it is worked. "I was very excited to try Beeswax and I am seeing other lampworkers getting great results. It did not disappoint. The Misty, more translucent, is on the right side of my hand, and the Milky, more opaque, is on the left. It strikes to yellow while you are working where it cools, and finishes striking in the kiln. I did find that the areas that struck before going in the kiln were deeper and richer in color after." – Dwyn Tomlinson

5WWXnu.name: Beeswax Milky
5WWXnu.description: A lemon milky opal yellow that can strike to a deeper amber depending on the time and temperature it is worked. "I was very excited to try Beeswax and I am seeing other lampworkers getting great results. It did not disappoint. The Misty, more translucent, is on the right side of my hand, and the Milky, more opaque, is on the left. It strikes to yellow while you are working where it cools, and finishes striking in the kiln. I did find that the areas that struck before going in the kiln were deeper and richer in color after." – Dwyn Tomlinson

2wvw3y.name: Cupcake
2wvw3y.description: A creamy off-white / yellow opaque. “Cupcake is a silver yellow. The batch I used is a milky ivory with no yellowing, similar to CiM Buttermilk and to Heather Sellers’ sample [above]. It is a stable ivory without the color separation [curdling] that distinguishes Effetre Ivory.” – Laurie Nessel

3FKH4Y.name: Alchemy
3FKH4Y.description: An opaque yellow with dark green streamers. “Here are two of six new complex opaque canes that CiM released in spring 2021. Four of them-Howlite, Alchemy, Alakazam and Dinosaur Bone- have a Buttermilk matrix and are absolutely perfect for depicting marble. The marbling in Alchemy is from Eel Grass [transparent green] and Eden [dense transparent pine green with aventurine] cane just below the surface of the cane. Another ‘marbleous’ CiM color!” – Laurie Nessel

51kxeG.name: Alakazam
51kxeG.description: An opaque yellow with turquoise blue & dark green streamers. “Alakazam is a complex opaque cane made of Fremen and Eden cane in a Buttermilk matrix. The base bead is Effetre Navy Blue. Alakazam is marbleous!” – Laurie Nessel

6MZbP0.name: Buttercup
6MZbP0.description: A bright transparent yellow. "I think Buttercup is my favorite translucent yellow. Not that there are many out there to choose from. Buttercup is bright true yellow, translucent, but it can opacify slightly depending on thickness/heat, I think. It can produce lovely striations in the yellow. Truly is smooth like butter." – Anna Miller

2ES0RC.name: Glimmer Misty
2ES0RC.description: A slightly greenish yellow misty opal. "Glimmer is a pretty opal translucence that accents colors used with it. Easy to work with; not shocky; no bubbling or scum. Did not react with ivory." – Beth Swain

3YK7qm.name: Celadon
3YK7qm.description: An opaque sea foam green. Click here to view Celadon Uniques Melanie uses Celadon frit in her blend "Trails." See more of her 104 compatible FrittyBits blends . – Melanie Graham

1NzsC3.name: Peacock Green
1NzsC3.description: A milky green moonstone. Click here to view Peacock Green Uniques "I made two beads of Peacock Green and Halong Bay. One bead of each color without striking, just formed a bead and put it in the kiln. And another bead of each color struck three times. That is, I cooled the bead until it stopped glowing, then slowly heated it and so on three times. The struck beads are obviously more milky and this glow is very noticeable. It's sooo beautiful!" – Olga Ivashina

0t42Cx.name: Elphaba
0t42Cx.description: An opaque lime green that is less reactive than other 104 pea greens. Click here to view Elphaba Uniques "Elphaba is a beautiful spring green. After some very minor encounters with the bright Effetre greens [Nile Green, Pea Green] I approached this colour thinking that it would be more aggressive with other colours, and streakier. I was pleasantly surprised! . . . Elphaba is a surprisingly soft colour. I'd rate its viscosity maybe a 1 or 2 on the scale where 0 is Effetre White and 10 is Effetre Black." Read more at Melanie's blog . – Melanie Graham

4eW2Hd.name: Mojito
4eW2Hd.description: A transparent yellowish green with grey overtones. Check out Jolene Wolfe's tutorial Making Lime Murrini which includes Mojito, Sherwood, and Cardamom. – Jolene Wolfe

4U8zfY.name: Slytherin
4U8zfY.description: A very dense and dark transparent mossy green. Click here to view Slytherin Uniques "As I am often doing beads to which I like to use transparent glass very thinly, I am interested in the saturation of glass colour. If the glass is dark it does not necessarily mean it is intense. I made test beads, first a basic bead using only the colour in question and then a white bead I covered quite thickly with the said glass. Ultimate test was a triangle bead using a couple of greens in it. Glass melts very thinly in the triangle beads and it is covered with clear [Effetre 006 in this case] which can kind of dilute it optically even more." Read more at Maikki's blog . – Maija-Leena Autio

35ze7B.name: Poison Apple
35ze7B.description: A bright milky opal green that stays translucent after annealing- same hue as Wheatgrass. "The new Poison Apple is fantastic! It really looks like nephrite Jade! It’s really a color I’ve been hoping for for a while. Here is a side-by-side comparison of old [top] and new [bottom] Poison Apple." – Alexis Berger

2y2A9j.name: Appletini
2y2A9j.description: A transparent bottle green. “These colored transparents are really really stiff, and when you’re encasing with them you really have to get them nice and hot. And don’t drag the glass- just lay it on top of stuff. Don’t drag it over, gently lay it on top. . . . Because if you try too hard, and you drag this really stiff transparent, you’re going to smudge your designs.” Watch Maria's YouTube demo encasing copper cut outs with Appletini. – Maria Schoenenberger

4cPba4.name: Emerald City
4cPba4.description: A transparent green. "On a base of Emerald City, this set of treasures was created with combinations of green and clear transparents and silver glasses including TAG's Taxco Silver Turquoise and Double Helix Gaia silver infused glass. Highlights of Double Helix Aurae create the glitter bling on each bead!" See more on Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

5jjEcG.name: Fiddlehead
5jjEcG.description: An opaque green. "On the mandrel you will see that bead has ivory dots, and there has been a nice reaction with the ivory and the Fiddlehead." Read more at Dwyn's blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

1f6RSc.name: 50s Kitchen
1f6RSc.description: An opaque green. "50s Kitchen Ltd Run rolled in 99% fine silver foil created a natural non-reactive base for a sprinkling of Glass Diversions Utopia glass frit. The silver droplets rise to the surface and frame the frit in a tapestry like look and feel. The silver seemed to bring out richer greens and darker hues of purple-browns." Read more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

31tu4q.name: Loch Ness
31tu4q.description: A deep green moonstone. "Silver dissolves in a fun way on top of Loch Ness, looking almost like a starscape or galaxy. When the silver is reduced and encased, it opacifies on top of the Loch Ness and develops hints of blue here and there. This colour has potential as a good base colour for silver glass. Both my reducing silver glass and my striking silver glass got great colour on top of it." Read more at Melanie's blog . – Melanie Graham

0nevSz.name: Limelight
0nevSz.description: A transparent green. "Next up, a simpler look of the encased silver glass reaction. The Double Helix Psyche glass was reduced and then encased with Limelight to capture the blues/ pinks and amber hues." Read more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

2FhufX.name: Primavera
2FhufX.description: An opaque green. Left to right: Primavera, Sherbert, Cardamom, Mint Chip, It Ain't Easy Being, Sprout, Apple Pie – Claudia Eidenbenz

73VfVq.name: Eucalyptus
73VfVq.description: An opaque pastel green. "It's a little more dense as well, making it easier to layer with, a lot like the consistency of Dirty Martini [one of my faves]. Eucalyptus works easily, without being shocky or too stiff. It doesn't seem to bleed at all. It does striate a little bit, but that goes away somewhat when encased or layered with a transparent color." Read more at Kandice's blog . – Kandice Seeber

3gHt4d.name: Ogre
3gHt4d.description: An opaque green. "Ogre with Reichenbach Magic dots and eyestalks. Its underside is still mostly green. The color developed as I kept reheating the body as I added the dots and eyes. Work, reheat, work, reheat." – Chris Haussler

4K7UxP.name: Leaf Men
4K7UxP.description: An opaque green. Left to right: Effetre 856, Army Men, Olive, Juniper, Leaf Men, Sherwood – Claudia Eidenbenz

0teSmz.name: Meadow
0teSmz.description: An opaque green. Left to right: Split Pea, Turtle Power, Effetre 853, Shrubbery, Effetre 299, Reichenbach 4201, Meadow – Claudia Eidenbenz

4rqhqp.name: Pistachio Ice Cream
4rqhqp.description: An opaque pale green. Check out Maria's YouTube demo making Groot with Pistachio Ice Cream. – Maria Schoenenberger

29aTHb.name: Musk
29aTHb.description: A transparent brown-ish green. "The top strung bead is Effetre Kelp, all the bottom beads are Musk." – Jean Daniels

66KXDf.name: Spearmint
66KXDf.description: An opal green. "Spearmint fills the hole that Mint Lozenge left!" – Trudi Doherty

6krTc1.name: Elf
6krTc1.description: An opaque green. "Elf appears to be an opaque medium blue-green that is similar to Effetre's Petroleum Green. The unworked rods have a shimmer to them [depending on the angle of the light] that does translate into the worked glass. This is a slightly streaky green." Read more at DragonJools blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

6PM9cE.name: Peridot
6PM9cE.description: A transparent gemstone green. "Peridot is a gorgeous transparent yellow-green. It’s clear as anything and I had no bubbling or scumming issues with it, but do bear in mind that I work everything slowly and quite cool. It’s a crisp, fresh green that doesn’t really have a glassy counterpart. It’s a bit like CiM Mojito but paler and more yellow. If you can remember the original Effetre transparent Pale Emerald green from yonks back [not the awful too-green one they do now], it’s like that, but with a touch of yellow to it. Just lovely." Read more at Laura's tumblr . – Laura Sparling

36mdEy.name: Refresh
36mdEy.description: A transparent light emerald green. "About eleven years ago, Effetre’s transparent Pale Emerald Green 031 was a thing of beauty and it used to be one of my absolute favourite glasses. The pale emerald which Effetre produces now is nice but, much like many things form yesteryear, it’s not the same as it used to be. However, CiM’s Refresh is an absolute dead ringer for that Effetre Pale Emerald Green of old and I love it. There are no bubbling or scumming issues and it’s not too stiff which makes it ideal for encasing. Unlike many other transparent pale greens, it has a definite blueness to it which I really like. Most other transparent pale greens have a yellowness to them." Read more at Laura's tumblr . – Laura Sparling

6tfpAM.name: Troll
6tfpAM.description: An opaque gray green. Check out Maria's YouTube demo making an apple with a worm in it using CiM Firecracker & Troll . – Maria Schoenenberger

12f7xr.name: Eel Grass
12f7xr.description: A nature-inspired transparent green. "Eel Grass is a very cool green. I work hot so it was bubbly. It's very natural, perfect for flowers! I tried putting it on top of white, it's very light, I like the result. I think it is a romantic light green." – Pauline Chevalier

5Sy2yR.name: Apple Pie
5Sy2yR.description: An opaque minty pastel green. A comparison of various CiM etched greens. – Heike Loos

6bm48F.name: Chrysalis
6bm48F.description: A dense opal green. "Chrysalis is very reactive with other colours. . . . Peace, Ivory, Opal Yellow, and Copper Green all separated on top of Chrysalis. The other interesting thing is the blotchiness that Chrysalis seems to cause both when used on top of other colours, curdling them, and when used underneath other colours, curdling itself." Read more at Melanie's blog . – Melanie Graham

2y7kqd.name: Jelly Bean
2y7kqd.description: A bright opal jelly bean green. "Jelly Bean is somewhat similar to Chartreuse in its glowing green, though is greener and less yellow, and is less transparent inside so the mandrel line is barely evident in these barrels. This is a soft colour when molten. Like many opalinos it can crack near the end of the rod when it cools, which is visible so you can melt it back in carefully when you next use the rod." Read more at Heather's blog . – Heather Kelly

5HQvXG.name: Turtle Power
5HQvXG.description: An opaque green. A comparison of various CiM etched greens. – Heike Loos

1q2kDU.name: Camouflage
1q2kDU.description: An opaque olive green with a hint of gray. "Camouflage is a medium green opaque glass. It's quite streaky, separating on itself in lacelike patterns, and this behaviour seems to be aggravated by the addition of silver, becoming more pronounced." Read more at Melanie's blog . – Melanie Graham

2PUfgP.name: Oobleck
2PUfgP.description: An opaque vibrant acid green. "This set of crystal and barrel shaped beads were created with stripes of the following colors: Ocher, an opaque yellow; Monarch, an opaque yellow orange; Budgerigar, a misty opal kiwi green; & Oobleck, an opaque vibrant acid green. Each bead was sprinkled with Val Cox rare Purple Rose made with Z-99 glass frit. I rarely use my small supply of this frit as it is no longer available for purchase. A few beads got a wrap of 99% fine silver wire which was melted in for a tactile feel." Read more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

4fE2D9.name: Amphibian
4fE2D9.description: An opaque pale slate green. A comparison of various CiM etched greens. – Heike Loos

3PUpWn.name: Peppermint Cream
3PUpWn.description: An opaque neutral ivory with a hint of green. "Just a quick post to show you the glass combination discovery using Double Helix stormed Clio over Peppermint Cream. Look at that reaction in the centre of each portal drop in the centre bead! Wow... gotta make more of these!" Read more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

3Any3D.name: Mantis
3Any3D.description: A vibrant lime green misty opal- same hue as Eclectus Parrot. A comparison of CiM greens. – Heather Sellers

3egGzY.name: Wheatgrass
3egGzY.description: A bright misty opal green- the same hue as Poison Apple. "I was able to coax a bit of opalescence out of Wheatgrass but I would call it a transparent color. It only started to gain some opacity after I worked it a whole bunch and that drop is relatively thick." – Alexis Berger

4zrren.name: Eden
4zrren.description: A dense transparent pine green with aventurine. “As you can see on the long bead, Eden is very dark. In a solid bead, you can't really see the color. But as soon as I apply it on white, I begin to see a nice deep green. I really like its hue! It is perfect for my Lotus style beads.” – Pauline Chevalier

5vVQQY.name: Weeping Willow
5vVQQY.description: A soft opaque green with a touch of gray. "Weeping Willow is a nice pale evergreen with dark striations throughout. Left bead is Weeping Willow. Right bead is Effetre Moss." See more at Jean's blog . – Jean Daniels

5eT4DM.name: Bayou
5eT4DM.description: An opaque gray-green. Left to right: CiM Troi, Bayou, Weeping Willow, Anole, Eclectus Parrot, & Wheatgrass. – Heike Loos

3jMJxa.name: Lady of the Lake
3jMJxa.description: A pale green milky opal that stays translucent after annealing- same hue as Sea Glass. Left to right: Sea Glass, Lady of the Lake. See more of Claudia’s color comparisons . – Claudia Eidenbenz

4eQ65m.name: Nymph
4eQ65m.description: A green misty opal- same hue as Persian Green. "Clear core, Canyon de Chelly case, Nymph torso- like butter, no reducing or scumming. Dreamy." – Laurie Nessel

0fcybH.name: Persian Green
0fcybH.description: A green milky opal that stays translucent after annealing- same hue as Nymph. "064 black base, Persian Green- like butter, viscous, resistant to reducing. Beautiful color." – Laurie Nessel

6BP53r.name: Avonlea
6BP53r.description: A bright green misty opal- same hue as Shamrock. Left to right: Avonlea, Shamrock. See more of Claudia’s color comparisons . – Claudia Eidenbenz

2d0A4p.name: Limeade
2d0A4p.description: A lemon-lime cloudy transparent. "This group featuring Avalon Milky [new personal favorite- left], Limeade [middle] and Beeswax Milky [right]. All of these play very nicely and aren't shocky like other semi-transparent colors." – Bling Squared Cute Glass

43brXw.name: Pond Slime Misty
43brXw.description: A yellowish green misty opal. "There is something magnetic about this translucent green shade. I love the way it transmits light. It melts smoothly and remains slightly stiff - perfect for sculpting as so many milky shades." – Anna Miller

2T6xj3.name: Pond Slime Milky
2T6xj3.description: A yellowish green milky opal. "Just like the Misty shade, just a little more opaque. Thin layers will give a transparent look. This colour shouts Spring. Easy, smooth and no bubbling." – Jean Daniels

0STdHa.name: Honeydew Milky
0STdHa.description: A pale green milky opal. “While quite similar to Pond Slime, Honeydew is slightly paler and not quite as yellow. I love the translucent softness of this shade. There were no issues with working this glass nor was it shocky. Honeydew is shown here in rod form, as a sculpted flower, encasing silver foil and encasing white.” – Janet Evans

72RK74.name: Winter Mint Misty
72RK74.description: A minty green misty opal. "Winter Mint Misty is a pretty minty green opal translucent. Easy to work with and the color intensifies with deeper layers. A slight reaction with ivory." – Beth Swain

73JerD.name: Kiwi Misty
73JerD.description: A lime green misty opal. "Kiwi Misty is a pretty pale lime green. I did get a little streaking. Not shocky; no bubbling; and did not react with ivory." – Beth Swain

4XUXge.name: Kiwi Milky
4XUXge.description: A lime green milky opal. "Kiwi Milky is a pale lime green opal color that intensifies with deeper layers. No distortion; not shocky; no bubbling; the milky color intensifies with deeper layers. Did not react with ivory." – Beth Swain

0b0EY7.name: Amazon Misty
0b0EY7.description: A green teal misty opal. "Amazon Misty is a pleasing green teal misty color. Easy to work with; no distortion; not shocky; no bubbling; did not react with ivory." – Beth Swain

0yPUFz.name: Amazon Milky
0yPUFz.description: A green teal milky opal. "Amazon Milky is a green teal opal color that intensifies with deeper layers. No distortion; not shocky; no bubbling. Did not react with ivory." – Beth Swain

664KZJ.name: French Blue
664KZJ.description: An opaque blue. "The glass I have used in Point Break is CiM French Blue, CiM Hades, Effetre Cobalt Lapis, Reichenbach Multicolor and a medley of blues in the ribbon cane." Read more at Kitzbitz Art Glass' blog . – Jolene Wolfe

463FvF.name: Leaky Pen
463FvF.description: An intense transparent ink blue. Check out Maria's YouTube video on Whirls Swirls & Twirls using a filigrana made with Effetre light blue and Leaky Pen. – Maria Schoenenberger

6kjjX5.name: Halong Bay
6kjjX5.description: A milky cobalt blue moonstone. "I made two beads of Peacock Green and Halong Bay. One bead of each color without striking, just formed a bead and put it in the kiln. And another bead of each color struck three times. That is, I cooled the bead until it stopped glowing, then slowly heated it and so on three times. The struck beads are obviously more milky and this glow is very noticeable. It's sooo beautiful!" – Olga Ivashina

6WXAPb.name: Lapis
6WXAPb.description: An opaque deep blue violet. Click here to view Lapis Uniques "Lapis is hands-down the best blue-purple opaque colour I've yet used. It is interestingly reactive, vibrant, and relatively inexpensive [compared to other purples and indigos] to boot." Read more at Melanie's blog . – Melanie Graham

1y6dxZ.name: Electric Avenue
1y6dxZ.description: An electric blue opal. Left to right: Atlantis, Effetre 356 dark turquoise alabaster, Tardis, Electric Avenue, Mermaid – Claudia Eidenbenz

6B5V7L.name: Chalcedony
6B5V7L.description: A periwinkle blue opal. Handmix of Chalcedony and Pink Champagne. – Gloria Sevey

2qBCFh.name: Pulsar
2qBCFh.description: An intense transparent aqua blue. "The bottom row contains the test beads of each of the nine glasses, the bottom bead of that glass alone, in the middle covered with clear and top on white. The beads on the other mandrel are my typical test beads that I do when I want to know how colorful some translucent glass is as a thin layer. Even though I tried to capture the colors as truthfully as possible, the shades are a little different than what they are in reality. At least on my screen." Read more at Maikki's blog . – Maija-Leena Autio

0gfAVp.name: Fremen
0gfAVp.description: An opaque sky blue. Click here to view Fremen Uniques "It is the unpleasant dirtiness that Effetre Dark Sky Blue and Dark Turquoise acquire in the flame that makes me prefer CiM Fremen and CiM Smurfy when I'm looking for a turquoise that is in this hue range. The CiM colours don't do this icky thing." – Melanie Graham

19waw5.name: Smurfy
19waw5.description: An opaque turquoise blue. "Smurfy is a medium to dark turquoise opaque colour. I found it really creamy and nice to work with, and vastly prefer it to the other dark turquoise opaques [Dark Turquoise, Dark Sky Blue] from Effetre because it doesn't easily develop that greyish dirty patina that other turquoises get, although you can make that happen if you really try. You can see in the bead on the left that when I reduced Smurfy it got a greyish haze on its surface. I reduced this bead a few times trying to get it to change colour. I was hoping for that solid red brick coating you can sometimes get on turquoises, but that doesn't seem to happen with this one." Read more at Melanie's blog . – Melanie Graham

59xm3A.name: Cornflower
59xm3A.description: An opaque cobalt blue. "This bicone was made with a bit more oxygen and marvered with a brass stump shaper instead. The colour is much clearer and has none of that smokey black trail [when using graphite]." Read more at DragonJools blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

1HuLWQ.name: Atlantis
1HuLWQ.description: A bluish teal opal. "Atlantis is described as a bluish teal opal which I think is quite accurate. This glass can vary in it's translucency depending on the amount of heat applied during the bead making process. In this set of beads, I paired it with Double Helix Aurae silver glass frit and I am pleased with these glittering rounds!" Read more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

3F39sK.name: Midnight
3F39sK.description: A dense transparent that color shifts between purple in daylight and navy blue in fluorescent light. "Midnight is a cool grey in my lotus style beads. I prefer bright colors with pep- but Midnight is a very cool neutral when used this way." – Pauline Chevalier

1pTgsW.name: Breeze
1pTgsW.description: A transparent teal. "Breeze is definitely my favourite of this trio, it is a deep, vibrant and happy true aqua colour. Here you can see Breeze encased with Effetre 006 clear. This colour is so gem-like and appealing that I'd love to see it become a permanent fixture in the CiM palette." Read more at Jo's Kitzbitz Art Glass blog . – Jolene Wolfe

6wgxGk.name: Blue-yah!
6wgxGk.description: A transparent blue. "And if you have ever looked at a bottle of Windex and thought - damn, I wish there was a glass that colour - well - there is. Blue-Yah!" Read more at DragonJools blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

4N1T9a.name: Moonlight
4N1T9a.description: A transparent steel blue. "Another colour I adore ... there's nothing else like it!" – Trudi Doherty

4a8zTE.name: Denim
4a8zTE.description: A transparent denim blue. "Greys are usually very light when layered thinly, even when they are dark in a rod. Anyway I decided to test the shades Mockingbird 822 and blue gray Denim 541 with some older grays I happen to have in the shelf. Other colours are Effetre 086 and 088 and CiM Twilight. Well, besides Denim all the glasses diluted to almost nonexistence, and Denim is classified as blue at CiM's homepage, but when layered heavy, we can see the different shades well. Eff 086 turns to brown, Eff 088 lightly to green. Mockingbird is neutral true gray, Denim blue gray of course and Twilight another true gray, close to Mockingbird, just a bit warmer." Read more at Maikki's blog . – Maija-Leena Autio

10Ccy6.name: Blue Arrow Frog
10Ccy6.description: A bright opaque blue. "Blue Arrow Frog is virtually indistinguishable from Effetre 242 Medium Lapis. How indistinguishable, you ask? Well - that bead has dots of Medium Lapis on it." Read more at DragonJools blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

2RmdqH.name: Barrier Reef
2RmdqH.description: A transparent teal. "As I am often doing beads to which I like to use transparent glass very thinly, I am interested in the saturation of glass colour. If the glass is dark it does not necessarily mean it is intense. I made test beads, first a basic bead using only the colour in question and then a white bead I covered quite thickly with the said glass. Ultimate test was a triangle bead using a couple of greens in it. Glass melts very thinly in the triangle beads and it is covered with clear [Effetre 006 in this case] which can kind of dilute it optically even more. Especially I liked the beautiful teal shade of Barrier Reef. It is too dark, almost black as itself, but they make nice triangle bead together, being in a blueish and yellowish end of green spectrum." Read more at Maikki's blog . – Maija-Leena Autio

5aXWkk.name: Prussian Blue
5aXWkk.description: An deep opaque blue laden with silver. "Prussian Blue is a much more intensely saturated navy blue than Class M Planet. The deep color has the same hint of mossy green, however the navy blue is much more intense under the exact same torch conditions. No shocking or bubbling occurred during testing." – Heather Sellers

05cuRT.name: Cotswold Blue
05cuRT.description: A muted opaque teal. "Copper Green, Ivory, and Opal Yellow all separate on top of Cotswold Blue. Cotswold Blue is such a streaky colour that it separates on top of everything. The only real reactions of note here were: -Ivory and Cotswold Blue form a mutual dark line reaction -The edges where Peace and Cotswold Blue meet get sort of fuzzy and translucent. You can see this in both beads." Read more at Melanie's blog . – Melanie Graham

0Mh1KR.name: Sacre Bleu
0Mh1KR.description: A bright transparent blue. "These beads use CiM Baked Alaska with fine silver swirls with CiM Sacre Bleu skies! That glittery moon is Double Helix Aurae. The blue is stunning in person and the beads found a home with a happy customer very quickly." Read more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

6dBkWZ.name: Merryweather
6dBkWZ.description: An opal blue. "Merryweather is a pretty blue opal glass. I sprinkled it with Fortune Teller Lumiere Lusters by JetAge Studios. . . . The color of Merryweather is a happy blue so looking forward to using it again in some future beads." Read more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

0Mm1vs.name: Troi
0Mm1vs.description: An opaque teal. "Troi is a vibrant medium teal opaque. It reminds me of Mermaid, only a bit lighter and bluer. I was a little unprepared for how vibrant it would be, because the rod colour is a little more subdued than this colour ends up being after working and annealing it. It's quite a streaky colour, leaving little trails and veins of darker teal all through it no matter how carefully you work. Like many other colours in the turquoise/teal families, you can get a brick red reduction on Troi. You sort of have to work at it, though, and the result I got was blotchy. I tried a variety of strengths of reduction flame, and a variety of flame-height positions while reducing this and was not able to achieve an even coverage. Maybe you'll have better luck?" Read more at Melanie's blog . – Melanie Graham

3WjL0x.name: Little Boy Blue
3WjL0x.description: A muted opaque blue with gray tones. "Reducing silver glass frit is pretty on top of Little Boy Blue, and it really stands out as an excellent base of striking silver glass frit. I got beautiful colour from my TerraNova2 here, and beautiful separation haloes around all the little fritty bits." Read more at Melanie's blog . – Melanie Graham

35eJPN.name: Montezuma
35eJPN.description: An opaque navy blue laden with silver. "Montezuma is an excellent jeans color." – Laurie Nessel

5NeKS6.name: Lunar
5NeKS6.description: A blue opal. "Lunar was an attempt to re-make Tardis and it's almost spot on. It's maybe a shade darker than Tardis, and Tardis might be ever so slightly greener, but they are very very similar. Easy to work and rather lovely to look at. The bubbles you can see in my photo are from using the glass at the cut end of the rod. I haven't noticed bubbles in beads made with glass further down the rod. I'm finding it really hard to photograph Lunar well. I keep getting reflections or marks and even coming back to it over several days hasn't helped." – Heather Johnson

4FdXPD.name: Carefree
4FdXPD.description: A clear base with green, purple, and blue streamers. "A really fun colour! Stripes of turquoise, pale green and purple. Pale green almost white opal shade. Nice melting and no bubbling. Neutral flame. Nice effects when worked in layers." – Jean Daniels

3tENWZ.name: Lake Baikal
3tENWZ.description: A transparent blue with subtle lavender wisps. "Pretty shade like a darker Larkspur or Bashful. Works so good in neutral flame with wisps of dark pink but looks orange. Pretty blue/lavender colour glass." – Jean Daniels

6rt8jR.name: Robert E.
6rt8jR.description: A transparent medium blue with excellent clarity. "Robert E. is actually a richer cobalt than pictured." – Laurie Nessel

5aeKxz.name: Carnival
5aeKxz.description: A light blue transparent base with reddish orange, yellow, green, and white streamers. "Orange and yellow ribbons are combined with a light blue transparent glass. As with all of the transparent based streamers, I like it best over another opaque glass. Shown here over white and as streamers." – Janet Evans

5jwrzW.name: Stonewashed
5jwrzW.description: A soft denim blue cloudy transparent. "The videos and other photos I see from people of Stonewashed make it look like a really glorious blue, and I see that even my own photos tend to make it look like a really wonderful shade of blue. In real life, it is more in keeping with its name, a stone washed denim colour, that is a blue-grey. The rod I tried was quite shocky, but not everyone is finding that." – Dwyn Tomlinson

3mek4S.name: Starry Night
3mek4S.description: An opaque creamy yellow with blue streamers. “My favorite of the new batch of colors, Starry Night [here used as the base bead] is the closest to the awesome Pachamama that sold out. The lines stay tight and crisp with normal heat. I prefer to distress it by raking, smearing, and blasting it in patches until it diffuses, creating a dreamy look.” – Laurie Nessel

611B82.name: Aquamarine Ice Misty
611B82.description: A cyan blue misty opal. "This is a lovely milky turquoise. Very light and almost glowing. Reminds me of the bright turquoise color of glacier ice. Easy to work, not shocky or boily [is that a word?] Very clean and stable color." – Anna Miller

3hsZhb.name: Aquamarine Ice Milky
3hsZhb.description: A cyan blue milky opal. "Aquamarine Ice Misty and Milky. The top fishy is the Misty. In the photos I look at it and think dark aqua or aqua or turquoise, but in real life I think they look not quite so aqua, more of a cyan." – Dwyn Tomlinson

0nxzUd.name: Arctic Milky
0nxzUd.description: A pale milky blue in rod form; once worked and annealed it turns a mossy green. "As many CiM testers have communicated, Arctic has not behaved as expected. In the rod it is a light blue milky opal. My testing results for Arctic Misty resulted in a dark bottle green brown when I paired it with silver glass. In anticipation of a similar result in testing the Milky version, I intentionally used Double Helix Aurae fine glass frit to create this set of beads. The spacers are solid Arctic Milky. It is a belief of mine that a kiln environment with silver glass present may be a clue to why this blue glass changes color so dramatically." See more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

5BHUqW.name: Fjord Misty
5BHUqW.description: A bluish teal misty opal. "This is Fjord Misty [top and left] and Milky [flowy-er tail]. The Milky appears lighter, but is thinner. I was having a lot of trouble with the rod shocking. Great color!" – Dwyn Tomlinson

0sYyv3.name: Fjord Milky
0sYyv3.description: A bluish teal milky opal. "This simple set of jewelry box beads was created on a base of CiM's Fjord Milky, a bluish teal milky opal, sprinkled with Val Cox Sadie Hawkins frit. Two crystal shapes, four rounds and two spacers make up this set." See more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

0EefJM.name: Niagara Misty
0EefJM.description: A slightly bluish teal misty opal. Left to right: Niagara Misty, Niagara Milky. – Claudia Eidenbenz

1KBXk1.name: Niagara Milky
1KBXk1.description: A slightly bluish teal milky opal. "Niagara Milky is a gorgeous blue from CiM in a bright, yet deep shade of blue. It's an opal glass that really has a luminous quality! It's soft to melt and easy to work with. I did briefly warm the end before using [habit] and it was fuss free." – Trudi Doherty

2M0BDx.name: Waimea Misty
2M0BDx.description: A teal misty opal. "I love this unique colour! Left to right pairs: 1/ Waimea Misty encased in SuperClear, rolled in frit and wrapped in fine silver wire 2/ Waimea Misty, dichro, SuperClear 3/ Waimea Misty, frit, SuperClear." – Sandra Beingessner

3kUxPk.name: Waimea Milky
3kUxPk.description: A teal milky opal. Left to right: Waimea Misty, Waimea Milky. – Claudia Eidenbenz

16RZdj.name: Delft Misty
16RZdj.description: A blue misty opal. "Delft Misty is a blue misty opal. Easy to work with. Not shocky; no bubbling; color intensifies with deeper layers. Did not react with ivory." – Beth Swain

61z15B.name: Delft Milky
61z15B.description: A blue milky opal. "Delft Milky is a blue milky opal. Easy to work with. Not shocky; no bubbling; color intensifies with deeper layers. Did not react with ivory." – Beth Swain

5GSkbc.name: Thai Orchid
5GSkbc.description: A dark, rich opaque purple. Melanie uses Thai Orchid frit in her blend "Go Van Gogh." See more of her 104 compatible FrittyBits blends . – Melanie Graham

2nHMh0.name: Count von Count
2nHMh0.description: A transparent color that shifts between blue and lavender depending on your lighting. Daylight Left to right: Trapeze, Enchanted, Jellyfish, Count von Count – Claudia Eidenbenz

0cSjKr.name: Eggplant
0cSjKr.description: A very dense and saturated opal purple. Vickie Christian uses Eggplant frit to create 104 compatible frit blends. Find more blends at Vickie's Emporium . – Vickie Christian

286Hpt.name: Crocus
286Hpt.description: A milky opal lavender that stays translucent after annealing- same hue as Wisteria. Click here to view Crocus Uniques Hillary Lawson created this gorgeous tutorial featuring CiM Firecracker, Crocus, & Wisteria. Visit Glass Alchemist for the video portion of the tutorial [and other tutorials as well]. – Hillary Lawson

5fsegR.name: Poi
5fsegR.description: An opaque grey purple. Poi with 99% fine silver wire. See more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

2b67TF.name: Dark Velvet
2b67TF.description: An intense transparent purple. "Dark Velvet is perfect for beads such as lotuses. When used on top of white and/or encased with a transparent, the color lightens. It is a nice - but actually very dark- purple. By working the color on the lotus style bead, I could see bubbles forming. I may have overheated it, but I find that the bubbles make it more fun." – Pauline Chevalier

3QAgez.name: Gypsy
3QAgez.description: An extremely dark transparent purple. "Use as dots, in stringer, over clear, wherever you need a deep, intense colour that can stand to be diluted a lot." Read more at DragonJools blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

6fxTM0.name: Coronation Day
6fxTM0.description: A dark opal purple. "Let's cover the details of the CiM glass colors: Ocher, an opaque yellow; Quetzal, an opaque blue with green undertones; Coronation Day, a dark opal purple. This created an amazing combination. Each glass melts smoothly, layered without issues and the silvered ivory stringer detail on the focal bead was beautiful." Read more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

21Neug.name: Boysenberry
21Neug.description: A dense and saturated purple moonstone. "Boysenberry is a very cool dark purple, I like the color when I put the bead into the light. On white it is perfect for a dark purple effect!" – Pauline Chevalier

2U4hqr.name: Aladdin
2U4hqr.description: A purple moonstone. "Aladdin is a mysterious purple which breathes new life in the flame. The rod appears slightly opal and muted, however the melt tells a different story. The purple glass becomes transparent with a kiss of vibrant magenta. Aladdin is a lovely component for murrini. No shocking or bubbling occurred during testing." – Heather Sellers

1KuXUT.name: Emperor
1KuXUT.description: A golden transparent purple. "I was not fond of Emperor the first couple of times I tried it. I couldn’t get any color at all. I work fast, hot, and small, which made this glass super uncooperative. It likes to be cool. In layers and large complicated beads it strikes fine. In small spacers and headpins, not so much. I've discovered you just need to be patient and let it cool down. Work with it like normal and ignore it until you need it to strike. Then let it cool until the glow is gone completely, to the point that it makes you nervous. Then strike it gently at the very edge of the flame. Watching the color bloom is so satisfying." – Dana Phillips

2EbjpX.name: Byzantium
2EbjpX.description: A purple moonstone. Byzantium with gold. – Pauline Chevalier

24dchn.name: Cleopatra
24dchn.description: A dense and saturated transparent purple. "Cleopatra is a deep purple, very dark. I prefer to work on top of white to reveal this beautiful color. Works with translucents too for a lighter purple!" – Pauline Chevalier

69ERFW.name: African Violet
69ERFW.description: A dense and saturated transparent indigo. "Not sure what I think of this colour. It's a lovely, soft, blue purple, lavender colour. It leans a little to the grayish end of the spectrum. I think I just expected it to have a little bit more oomph. I think it wants to be layered over other colours. You can see that I had a little bit of trouble with it boiling too, but that's probably just me and my super hot torch." Read more at DragonJools blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

6jzNQn.name: Bashful
6jzNQn.description: A transparent greyish purple. "It does appear to be a slightly different colour as a worked/annealed glass than as an unworked rod. I also had a tendency to air bubbles. Just couldn't get away from the tiny swirls of very small bubbles." Read more at DragonJools blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

3KAyAB.name: Enchanted
3KAyAB.description: A pink lavender transparent. "The side beads in this set are on bases of Enchanted- a pink lavender transparent. I dotted it with Double Helix Clio and encased the bead in clear. I like that when the base glass was paired with silver infused glass, the peachy pink cast of Clio over the purple hue is a nice compliment to the focal bead." Read more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

6rQ4hr.name: Rapunzel
6rQ4hr.description: An opaque lavender pink. "Rapunzel looks more purple or more pink, depending on the color of the light. I was thinking of it as a pink but there is a light purple vibe for sure." – Dwyn Tomlinson

2UeDun.name: Wisteria
2UeDun.description: A misty opal lavender- same hue as Crocus. "Wisteria is so beautiful when blown." – Suzy Hannabuss

0tmem3.name: Amethyst
0tmem3.description: A pale transparent pinky-purple. "I added a little bit of white enamel powder mixed in to give Amethyst a bit more translucency. That really helped bring out the delicate pale purple." – Alexis Berger

6Tw1VW.name: Your Majesty
6Tw1VW.description: A reddish pinky transparent purple. Your Majesty with gold. – Pauline Chevalier

5VdJkG.name: Bewitched
5VdJkG.description: A clear base with indigo and purple streamers. "Bewitched has suuuper subtle ribbons of light purple that are encased in transparent clear glass. Not my favourite, but I’m more of a vibrant colours kind of person. Shown here as spacers and over white." – Janet Evans

1pw1Jg.name: Yours Truly
1pw1Jg.description: A pinkish purple transparent with a wide variety of color results, depending on your working atmosphere. A comparison of our newest transparents. – Laurie Nessel

3Dzxhn.name: Kismet
3Dzxhn.description: A clear base with pink and purple streamers. "Thought I’d try it wrapped over black, as well as the self-wrapped bead. You can see the strands . . . but it’s kinda subtle. My camera picked up interesting diffusion of light in its shadow!" – Jenefer Ham

32qcCx.name: Lavender Storm
32qcCx.description: A clear base with pink and purple streamers.

2A7v6b.name: Douglas Aster
2A7v6b.description: An opaque pale lavender purple. Douglas Aster as stringer. – Caroline Davis

1Z3B6K.name: Pizzazz
1Z3B6K.description: A misty opal that color shifts between pink-purple and blue-purple depending on your lighting. "Pizzazz is a knockout! A smooth clear amethyst and lavender shade. Easy melting and shaping. I love this flowery colour." – Jean Daniels

0k51YS.name: Fairy Tale
0k51YS.description: A transparent color that shifts between blue and lavender depending on your lighting. "Well this one turned out a little surprisingly. In rod form it's purple, but as you can see once worked it shifts to a definite warm pink. I didn't notice any striking while working it. As you can see I have etched one of the beads, and it's very pretty either way! I did find that this needed to be worked a little cooler to prevent any bubbling, but it was only very slight and not a big issue." – Trudi Doherty

6yXhwW.name: Charisma
6yXhwW.description: A transparent lavender purple. "Charisma is an attractive lavender transparent that is quick melting. Easy to work with; not shocky; no bubbling or scum. Did not react with ivory." – Beth Swain

0aq1Ns.name: Aubergine Misty
0aq1Ns.description: A purple misty opal. "Aubergine Misty is a pale transparent opal purple that is easy to work with and not shocky; no bubbling or scum. Did not react with ivory." – Beth Swain

3j6MqJ.name: Aubergine Milky
3j6MqJ.description: A purple milky opal. "Aubergine Milky is a pale opal dusty purple that is easy to work with; not shocky; no bubbling or scum. Color intensifies with deeper layers. Did not react with ivory." – Beth Swain

1yfxwB.name: Butter Pecan
1yfxwB.description: A creamy opaque beige, less reactive than the ivories, that makes an excellent neutral base color. Click here to view Butter Pecan Uniques "Butter Pecan is the ultimate Caucasian skin tone. So creamy and easy to work with, with a nice, even finish." – Bling Squared Cute Glass

2bF3We.name: Ginger
2bF3We.description: A creamy opaque tan, less reactive than the ivories, that makes an excellent neutral base color. Click here to view Ginger Uniques "Ginger is a pretty, soft peachy-pink opaque colour. It is fairly inert - it will fume and discolour with silver, but in a much milder way than other neutral colours like Ivory. Ginger doesn't change colour when you reduce it. You can see in the bead here that Ginger can be a bit streaky. In that bead, a lot of the colour migrated to the middle of the bead when I was melting it down." Read more at Melanie's blog . – Melanie Graham

59bfyu.name: Chai
59bfyu.description: An opaque brown. Click here to view Chai Ltd Run Uniques “While the rod is a little darker than the last time around, the beads came out pretty similar. The leaf - which is cooled rapidly by mashing and then reheated along the edges, has some much more interesting colour variations.” Read more at DragonJools blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

6gU756.name: Sand Dollar
6gU756.description: An opaque light gray. Formerly Unique Ginger -3. “I love making these ocean critter beads, the sandy beach effect is really pretty I think. I make this look by wrapping Sand Dollar Ltd Run with silver leaf and then vapourising it in the flame.” Read more at Kitzbitz Art Glass’ blog . – Jolene Wolfe

22wsFU.name: Moccasin
22wsFU.description: An opaque brown. Left to right: Toto, Canoe, Safari, Moccasin – Claudia Eidenbenz

5PQcJC.name: Toto
5PQcJC.description: An opaque brown. Watch Maria make a bulldog with Toto on YouTube . – Maria Schoenenberger

5ytrSt.name: Ceylon
5ytrSt.description: A transparent brown. "Ceylon is a pretty good base colour for silver glass - both for the reducing colours and the striking ones. If you blow up the picture, you can see interesting effects in my reducing silver glass and lots of colour in the TerraNova2 frit." Read more at Melanie's blog . – Melanie Graham

6qdnSC.name: Velveteen
6qdnSC.description: A creamy light brown opal. "Velveteen on its own, the beads on each side of the focal bead, is a really interesting glass that creates striations of darker brown." Read more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

6YKusX.name: Safari
6YKusX.description: A yellow-toned opaque brown. Left to right: Toto, Canoe, Safari, Moccasin – Claudia Eidenbenz

6hE3dJ.name: Van Dyke Brown
6hE3dJ.description: An opaque dark brown. "Honestly - I can't tell them apart. Maybe Van Dyke [rod and 3 pieces on the left] retains a little more grey vs Safari [rod and 3 pieces on the right]. But functionally - I can't tell them apart. Maybe they work differently in beads. They are beautiful, but they seem interchangeable to me - given their variability." Read more at DragonJools blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

70Z5G2.name: Canoe
70Z5G2.description: An opaque silver brown. "This is Canoe from @creationismessy. It's a rich and warm colour which does lovely things with silvered ivory stringer. It strikes in the flame to create some really nice shades. I like this one a lot!" – Heather Johnson

5W0FLh.name: Burnt Sugar
5W0FLh.description: A warm transparent brown with a peachy blush. “Pretty transparent red/brown shade. Crystal clear and melting so smooth. Cooler shade goes well with blues and greens. Beads left to right: Maple, Horehound, Effetre light Topaz, Brown Eyed Girl, Burnt Sugar, and Indian Summer.” – Jean Daniels

31LKaZ.name: Bird's Nest
31LKaZ.description: A clear base with orange, yellow, green & black streamers. “Ribbons of black, pale yellow, orange and green. Reminds me of all the twigs and strings that our feathered friends use to make their homes. I got two different shades. One a warm yellow shade and another a cool clear tan. Love this so much!” – Jean Daniels

0Kfe7z.name: Brown Eyed Girl
0Kfe7z.description: A saturated true transparent brown. “Smooth clear transparent brown. Teeny tiny wisps in the glass. I found that Horehound and Brown Eyed Girl are so close that the difference was in the wisps. Beads from left to right: Maple, Horehound, Effetre light Topaz, Brown Eyed Girl, Burnt Sugar, and Indian Summer.” – Jean Daniels

3afHc9.name: Horehound
3afHc9.description: A pale transparent brown with yellow undertones. “Like the colour of those herbal candies. So close to Brown Eyed Girl. Crystal clear and smooth melting. Lovely autumn shade. Beads left to right: Maple, Horehound, Effetre light Topaz, Brown Eyed Girl, Burnt Sugar, and Indian Summer.” – Jean Daniels

526Acn.name: Grand Canyon
526Acn.description: An opaque brownish yellow with blue streamers. “Beads at bottom from left to right: Canoe, Serengeti, and Grand Canyon. Grand Canyon has lots of colourful striations of ochre, orange, yellow, and browns like the levels of natural sandstone. This is going to be my go-to for many applications. Got to try some leaves.” – Jean Daniels

4jFtee.name: Saddle Leather
4jFtee.description: A warm opaque brown. "A beautiful tan colour with hints of reddish brown in creases. A brown so natural as nature is. I love the smooth working and melting of this glass. A new addition to my acorns for fall." – Jean Daniels

6CDEpt.name: Café Au Lait
6CDEpt.description: A creamy opaque neutral with a touch of gray, laden with silver. "I tried Café Au Lait with dark turquoise, no reaction." – Dwyn Tomlinson

70VCW3.name: Bear Hug Misty
70VCW3.description: A brown misty opal. "Bear Hug Misty is a deep root beer brown. Easy to work with; not shocky; no bubbling or scum. Did not react with ivory." – Beth Swain

0JK7Ey.name: Bear Hug Milky
0JK7Ey.description: A brown milky opal. "Bear Hug Milky is a deep brown color that intensifies with depth. Easy to work with; not shocky; no bubbling or scum. Did not react with ivory." – Beth Swain

1uKaCk.name: Cirrus
1uKaCk.description: A milky white moonstone. Click here to view Cirrus Uniques "1 is the 2022 batch of Cirrus without striking, 2 is the 2022 batch struck three times, 3 the 2021 batch struck three times. The degree of milkiness is achieved by striking- in fact, I controlled the degree of milkiness by the number of strikes." – Olga Ivashina

0664P0.name: Hades
0664P0.description: An intense black that stays true black even when pulled into stringers and has spectacular reactions with silver. Click here to view Hades Uniques "Moretti black has been out at all distributors so after reading your testimonials I decided to try Hades....and OMG!!!! So excited! I was so shocked that it was just as dark as intense black. Hades just makes my beads POP with color." – Molly Cooley

1b98Z9.name: Clear
1b98Z9.description: A clear glass that prefers to be worked cool. “Wow! Look at the difference huh?! Pickling makes a HUGE difference in clarity for sure! You will still need to wipe down your rods with a CLEAN cloth and either window cleaner or alcohol before using because even though the rods have the grime cleaned off of them the oils on your skin will still make the glass scuzzy if you don't use clean rods.” Read more at Genea’s blog . – Genea Crivello

52kDzF.name: Peace
52kDzF.description: A dense opaque white, slightly stiffer & denser than other 104 whites. "Peace is the best white ever. It's so creamy . . . and super duper white. I like that." Watch Maria's polar bear demo on YouTube . – Maria Schoenenberger

2CddPD.name: Tuxedo
2CddPD.description: A regular black. "I tested Onyx, Tuxedo, and Hades to see which one holds the black the best. I like Tuxedo the best for stringer use. It holds the line pretty well." – Suzanne Cancilla-Fox

551Stv.name: Adamantium
551Stv.description: An opaque warm dark grey. Click here to view Adamantium Uniques "This set used Adamantium with Double Helix Helios handmade shards. When reduced, lots of blue was revealed in the shards which is a beautiful contrast to the grey base glass." See more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

4AVSe5.name: Jupiter Storm
4AVSe5.description: An opaque gray that strikes orange. Left to right: Foam, Coconut Milk, Bone, Jupiter Storm, Linen – Claudia Eidenbenz

0rRyFN.name: Mockingbird
0rRyFN.description: A transparent gray. "Greys are usually very light when layered thinly, even when they are dark in a rod. Anyway I decided to test the shades Mockingbird 822 and blue gray Denim 541 with some older grays I happen to have in the shelf. Other colours are Effetre 086 and 088 and CiM Twilight. Well, besides Denim all the glasses diluted to almost nonexistence, and Denim is classified as blue at CiM's homepage, but when layered heavy, we can see the different shades well. Eff 086 turns to brown, Eff 088 lightly to green. Mockingbird is neutral true gray, Denim blue gray of course and Twilight another true gray, close to Mockingbird, just a bit warmer." Read more at Maikki's blog . – Maija-Leena Autio

4Jmx93.name: Pachyderm
4Jmx93.description: A opaque grey laden with silver. "Pachyderm is one of my hands down favorite colors! The best grey with brown hues!" – Tammy Mercier

5HRQZq.name: Bone
5HRQZq.description: A pale opaque neutral. Left to right: Birchwood, Bone, Café Au Lait, Effetre ivory 264, Effetre dark ivory 276. – Bianca Gruber

1e7PZk.name: Tahitian Pearl
1e7PZk.description: A gray based metallic black. "Although Tahitian Pearl is most alluring for its iridescent surface, I found it to be by far the perfect [and only] color to simulate whale skin after being encased in clear. I've tried all the other grays and blacks and they were either too light, too black, too brown, or turned purple, or disintegrated and bled. When TP is incased, the sheen disappears and is replaced with a natural, mottled intensely dark gray. Using a black core for the whale, I've managed to make that one rod encase 7 whales with enough for about 5 more! It may be glass but it's like gold to me. I used Denim and Midnight in the top half to encase the base color." – Laurie Nessel

4rM2Y9.name: Porpoise
4rM2Y9.description: An opaque gray with a hint of green. "Porpoise is an almost neutral grey, with that ability to look different, depending on the surrounding colors. With black, it looks pure grey, but takes on a bluish or greenish tone if next to those colours. It's a nice colour to work, and it really does make me think of porpoises and dolphins." Read more at DragonJools blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

3fb1Tj.name: London Fog
3fb1Tj.description: A misty opal white - same hue as Unicorn. "I love Cirrus, London Fog, Swan and Unicorn!" – Suzy Hannabuss

0L3AkJ.name: Unicorn
0L3AkJ.description: A milky opal white that stays translucent after annealing- same hue as London Fog. "I love Cirrus, London Fog, Swan and Unicorn!" – Suzy Hannabuss

0crz9P.name: Onyx
0crz9P.description: A dense and shiny black. "I tested Onyx, Tuxedo, and Hades to see which one holds the black the best. I like Tuxedo the best for stringer use. It holds the line pretty well." – Suzanne Cancilla-Fox

1Xtt8H.name: Gossamer
1Xtt8H.description: A misty opal white. Lumen is on top, Gossamer on bottom. – Jolene Wolfe

168hyY.name: Dinosaur Bone
168hyY.description: An opaque yellow with orange & purple streamers. "Bleeding black isn't a result of your black, but rather the white you're using with it. Want to stop the bleeding of your black? Change your white! Try CiM Dinosaur Bone! It's similar in tonality to a light ivory, but it's stiffer than CiM Peace. Dino Bone doesn't spread when it gets hot, so it also doesn't bleed under the outside edges of your dots defusing your color, so it helps locking in your edges and keeping your lines nice and crisp!" – Hillary Lawson

6RxvhR.name: Howlite
6RxvhR.description: An opaque ivory with pale blue streamers. "Howlite was really easy to work with, it flowed well, which was a nice change over Peace. [Peace I generally love when I need a lot of detail and little movement.] Here is Howlite with silver foil." – Hillary Lawson

2xHuRr.name: Diaphanous Misty
2xHuRr.description: An ivory misty opal with a peach undertone. "Diaphanous Misty 841, on the left, and 842 Milky, on the right. I think the Milky does look a little bit milkier than the Misty. Very pretty." – Dwyn Tomlinson

2KtG68.name: Diaphanous Milky
2KtG68.description: An ivory milky opal with a peach undertone. "Diaphanous Misty 841, on the left, and 842 Milky, on the right. I think the Milky does look a little bit milkier than the Misty. Very pretty." – Dwyn Tomlinson

3USZLA.name: Glycerin Milky
3USZLA.description: An off-white milky opal. "Glycerin - this ghostly color really takes on the color of the light around it, showing a blue or yellow cast depending on the light source. It was the most amazing shade of gold when it was hot." – Dwyn Tomlinson

46H6yB.name: Birchwood
46H6yB.description: A creamy opaque ivory with silver. "Birchwood is an ivory, a little streaky, not too much, some color variation from heating, I really like this. Birchwood is super soft, so for the sculptural stuff, it can be a little tricky to hold the detail." – Dwyn Tomlinson

4KEqvK.name: Lychee Misty
4KEqvK.description: An ivory misty opal. "Lychee Misty is a pale ivory opalescence; easy to work with; not shocky; no bubbling or scum. Did not react with ivory." – Beth Swain

2w5Rb1.name: Lychee Milky
2w5Rb1.description: An ivory milky opal. "I made a sculptural bird bead with Lychee Milky. I began with a clear 'core' body and encased in Lychee Milky. This gives an opportunity to see encasement. The head, wings and tail were added straight from the rod. I used Reichenbach Deep Black for the base of the beak followed by Effetre Pastel Yellow. The eyes are also Reichenbach Deep Black." – Kim Fields

5HnZP0.name: Volcanic Ash Misty
5HnZP0.description: A grey misty opal. "Volcanic Ash Misty is easy to work with; no distortion; not shocky; no bubbling. The milky gray color intensifies with deeper layers. Did not react with ivory." – Beth Swain

6q9hSK.name: Volcanic Ash Milky
6q9hSK.description: A gray milky opal. Left to right: Volcanic Ash Misty, Volcanic Ash Milky. – Claudia Eidenbenz

5DqpbY.name: Gellys Sty
5DqpbY.description: A creamy, smooth and vibrant true opaque pink. Click here to view Gellys Sty Uniques "Gelly's Sty on the left, Dark Pink Alabastro on the right. Both pink. Both nothing alike." Read more at DragonJools blog . – Dwyn Tomlinson

36aSpL.name: Tutu
36aSpL.description: A pale transparent pink. "Tutu with encased Double Helix Terra2 which produced shining mother of pearl pinky goodness." Read more at Darlene's blog . – Darlene Collette

5zBxXU.name: Charlotte
5zBxXU.description: A transparent pink. Daylight Left to right: Sakura, Venus, Paris, Charlotte – Claudia Eidenbenz

1Qb2nN.name: Paris
1Qb2nN.description: A transparent pink. "I have been wanting to find a colour like Paris for some time. This soft peachy tone would pair very well with CiM Ginger." – Sandra Beingessner

160kWF.name: Venus
160kWF.description: A transparent pink with orange undertones. "Venus by itself is a lovely peachy shade. I find it easier to work with than many other translucent colours as it does not seem to mind being worked quite hot. There was very little in the way of scumming or micro bubbles due to boiling in a very hot flame." Read more at Kitzbitz Art Glass' blog . – Jolene Wolfe

2EeKLZ.name: Lilac
2EeKLZ.description: An opaque bubble gum pink with a blush of lavender. "Reducing silver glass is very pretty on top of Lilac, with the fritty bits developing interesting halos and fuming the Lilac an uneven yellowish colour. As a base for striking silver glass, Lilac is unremarkable." Read more at Melanie's blog . – Melanie Graham

1Qm0RE.name: Heather
1Qm0RE.description: A cloudy transparent pinkish purple. "I love this glass. In my opinion, it’s just as lovely as Effetre’s Evil Purple, but without the evil. It’s easy to work with on so many levels. It was not shocky poppy- didn't devitrify and didn't burn up.” – Susan Parry

2d030b.name: Ballerina
2d030b.description: A misty opal bright pink- same hue as Peony. "Ballerina is a very delicate pink that is really great to work with. I encased it in super clear." – Sandra Beingessner

3P4Bud.name: Dollhouse Misty
3P4Bud.description: A misty opal pink. "I decided to create a gummy bear with Dollhouse Misty and it did not disappoint. Lovely pink, I think my favorite! It has an internal glow to it, it flashes pink light when reflecting sun rays- just lovely!" – Anna Miller

2e9zGk.name: Dollhouse Milky
2e9zGk.description: A milky opal pink. Left to right: Diaphanous Misty, Diaphanous Milky, Ballet Slipper, Inca Rose, Ballerina, Dollhouse Misty, Dollhouse Milky, Gelly's Sty. – Bianca Gruber

04zmWK.name: Coming Up Roses
04zmWK.description: A transparent purplish pink with a wide variety of color results, depending on your working atmosphere and lighting. "Coming Up Roses had some air channels in the slightly off-shape rods which could indicate problems with the glass, but the bubbles were easy to pluck out and the glass ended up just fine. The color is gorgeous." – Laurie Nessel

1BQgsV.name: Pink Pansy
1BQgsV.description: A gold transparent ruby pink. "I layered Pink Pansy over number 204 white moretti. This rich pink is nice to work with and doesn’t tend to burn as easily as Rubino Oro. I will definitely be using more of this." – Sandra Beingessner

2QYjuK.name: Lingonberry
2QYjuK.description: A very saturated gold transparent ruby pink. "My take on Lingonberry is that it is a little darker than Pink Pansy, but side by side, I am not so sure. I did a better job of not getting that orange cast to the glass, but I have to say, I really cranked up the oxygen." – Dwyn Tomlinson

19fAaD.name: Elegance
19fAaD.description: A bubble gum pink that opacifies as you work it. "Elegance is a delicious cotton candy pink shade. The rods are more translucent as it appears to opacify a little during long working in the flame. I made a flower focal and a gummy bear. The focal was worked much longer then the gummy bear, and the gummy bear stayed more translucent." – Anna Miller

4te5T8.name: Ballet Slipper
4te5T8.description: A soft and pale cloudy transparent pink. "Ballet Slipper is a cloudy transparent colour. It's a beautifully soft pink with a touch of peach that gives a warm tone. I was pleasantly surprised as it looked paler in the rod, and despite these beads being relatively small [14 x 9 mm], the colour has certainly bloomed. Here it looks like a solid colour, and I'd like to experiment a bit more layering this over white to see if the pigment effect becomes more visible. As cloudy colours contain inclusions, I pre-heat these prior to use, [not for long] and I had no issues using it." – Trudi Doherty

0QV06k.name: Inca Rose
0QV06k.description: A peachy pink cloudy transparent. "Delicate warm pink, almost salmony pink. Light and translucent with great working characteristics, smooth and pliable, yet stays in place when sculpting." – Anna Miller

0E7Qs9.name: Bubble Pink
0E7Qs9.description: A transparent pink with micro bubbles. Left to right: Peony, Bubble Pink. – Claudia Eidenbenz

52YnKT.name: Bone
52YnKT.description: Summary: Technical. Description: Oracle Pastel test batch. Bone colored glass, can react with silver colors. The Oracle project gives 104 flame workers the option to use responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses in their work. All of our Oracle glasses are made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium.

1eZb8K.name: Violet
1eZb8K.description: Summary: Technical. Description: Oracle violet pastel test batch.
