3zh71S.name: Oracle-804.AuOpl
3zh71S.description: Summary: Pink fast opal. Description: Oracle-804.AuOpl , a pink fast opal. This opal is a striking glass that produces a range of misty opal pink tones. It easily resets to crystal clear, initiating the striking process. After resetting, it will cool to a faint translucent opalescence. This opal is “fast” compared to our regular oracle opal, and it will develop substantial opacity when annealed at 920F. For Best Results: Reset the Opal before annealing at 920°F for up to two hours. A translucent, opalescent strike will occur at these annealing temperatures. Higher temperatures and longer annealing times will initiate further striking of the opal. Encasing the Opal will also add heat and time so adjust your annealing accordingly or plan on having more opacity. The Beads: the horizontal bead is a wigwag bead with Oracle-802.AuOpl and Zephyr. The vertical bead is a wigwag of Zephyr and cane of 802.AuOpl encased in Zephyr.

2DX9nT.name: Oracle-803.AuOpl

It easily resets to transparent pale purple. After resetting, it will cool to a faint translucent opalescence. This opal is “slow” compared to our regular oracle opal, and it may require very gentle flame striking or longer annealing times or higher annealing temperatures to develop substantial opacity. For Best Results: Reset the Opal before annealing at 920°F for two hours or more. A translucent, opalescent strike can occur at annealing temperatures above 920F. Higher temperatures and longer annealing times will initiate further striking of the opal. The opal strike may also be initiated by resetting, cooling, and striking in a very cool flame before annealing. The Bead: is a wigwag bead with Oracle-803.AuOpl+Zephyr cane and Zephyr encasement dots.

68Cfc1.name: Oracle-752.opl
68Cfc1.description: Summary: Was sold at $30/pound.. Description: 752.opl – An opal glass that strikes in the flame and kiln. Compared to the 740/743.opl it is slower striking, and more translucent after annealing. 752.opl can be worked hot and fast in the torch flame. Working notes: -To retain the transparent opal effect, limit kiln temperature and annealing time. I use 920F for up to two hours for misty-opal beads. Clear encasement seems to accelerate opacification in the annealer. Kilns vary in the amount of heat at the beads’ location vs the displayed temperature. Your kiln is probably different than mine. Test beads are recommended. -A Reset/Cooling/Striking cycle can be used in the flame to alter the appearance of the opal effect. An encased bead that has been reset, air-cooled for 45 seconds, then very gently struck for 45 seconds seems to maintain the opalescent effect better than a bead annealed directing after resetting. The 752.opl’s reset and striking temperatures are lower than that of silver glasses. When reset, the glass is crystal clear, and when fully struck the glass is a milky opaque white. Variable opacity can be produced by controlling the thermal history of the workpiece. 1VC5KS.description: A dense version of our Chocolate Opal, this color looks purple or brown in different lights.

0wHLxT.name: Chocolate Opal
0wHLxT.description: Chocolate Opal features many vibrant hues that shift in different light spectrums, from deep purple to brilliant brown.

66Kbgg.name: Creme Brulee
66Kbgg.description: A Creamy color that can be used in multiple applications.

2ud46e.name: Dark Wildberry Satin
2ud46e.description: Darker variety of Wildberry with satin chatoyancy. This shade is nice and dark when solid, and can be sleeved or thinned for a more transparent or translucent finish.

1UBeGU.name: Dense Glopal
1UBeGU.description: This is a odd batch of dense Glopal rod with a slight satin.

40YUk6.name: Dense Orange Opal (Unique)
40YUk6.description: This is a dense opal orange color with slight satin. Best worked in a gentle flame or encased.

2LwV7f.name: Dense Pineapple Juice
2LwV7f.description: This is a lovely dense cadmium yellow based color.

6CWKak.name: Dense Rose Quartz
6CWKak.description: Dense Rose Quartz is a dense version Rose Quartz with extra milky opal effect. Under CFL it goes to a more intense electric hot pink.

0bcxBs.name: Diet Blue Cheese (Variant)
0bcxBs.description: This is a variant of our diet blue cheese. A lighter version of our classic blue cheese.

560JXG.name: Euro
560JXG.description: A clear that glows blue under UV.

1vkEPz.name: Exp. Black Pearl
1vkEPz.description: Experience the beauty of the Exp. Black Pearl Rod - a stunning, rod with an opalescent finish and a satin feel. Slowly pre heat rod and work it gently.

3yjEnG.name: Exp. Black
3yjEnG.description: Greasy Glass black rod. Our black consists of a super dense Wildberry variable. When thinned or exposed to bright backlight the color can show blue/purple. Keep dense for the most black affect.

25PMmR.name: Exp. Blood Orange
25PMmR.description: Vibrant transparent orange. There are some subtle variations in the strike from yellow to red and orange.

2jSSZF.name: Exp. Blood Red
2jSSZF.description: Bright yet deep toned transparent red rod that really pops.

1kYPU1.name: Exp. Blood Red (unique)
1kYPU1.description: Bright yet deep transparent red rod that really pops. This unique batch varies slightly in tone from the original, almost in the direction of a red orange though still definitely in the Blood Red family.

0RtMdx.name: Exp. Blue Phoenix
0RtMdx.description: A blue striking opal color that produces a range of hues from red to purple.

5TCTwC.name: Exp. Blueberry Opal
5TCTwC.description: This is a navy blue color in the same family as sonic.

6u0YhX.name: Exp. Bronze Pearl
6u0YhX.description: A Stunning experimental bronze colored extremely metallic looking color with opalescence to rival a pearl. Bronze Pearl shimmers and shines like a brilliant sparkle color, and also contains depth from the opal effect. This unique batch may have variations in color, and crystal size.

24nfhb.name: Exp. Cinnabar
24nfhb.description: A dense orange cadmium based color.

6Gz8Ek.name: Exp. Coral
6Gz8Ek.description: This is a cadmium based orange that looks similar to the marine invertebrates at the bottom of the sea.

0prpDa.name: Exp. Coraline Satin
0prpDa.description: Coraline Satin is a cadmium red satin color worked best in a gentle flame or encased. This is a limited batch available while supplies last.

0Y1JwG.name: Exp. Cosmos
0Y1JwG.description: A silver striking black that produces a range of colors.

2vbBhH.name: Exp. Dark Blue Raspberry
2vbBhH.description: Intriguing dark striking rod combining a medium saturation cobalt blue and a strong transparent ruby that strikes in the flame as well as the kiln.

43ZFB6.name: Exp. Dark Green Pearl
43ZFB6.description: Similar to Bronze Pearl, this Experimental Dark Green version appears dark and mysterious.

55gPt8.name: Exp. Dense Coral (variant)
55gPt8.description: This is similar to our coral but a little bit more opaque. Best worked in a gentle flame or encased.

0KAsbg.name: Exp. Dense Green Opal
0KAsbg.description: A cadmium based green opal that is a tad more dense than our Exp. Green Opal. This color works best in neutral to oxidizing flames or encased. This is the only batch of Dense Green Opal from 2025.

0G5e6v.name: Exp. Dense Yellow Opal
0G5e6v.description: This is a vivid yellow with opal qualities. Color works best in a neutral to oxidizing flame or encased.

0sAqh4.name: Exp. Dense Yellow Opal (unique)
0sAqh4.description: This Exp. Dense Yellow Opal Rod is an ideal choice for a one-of-a-kind piece. Its unique mustard color and dense opal structure provide a visually striking effect.

0eSESh.name: Exp. Desert Rose
0eSESh.description: This is a cadmium-based orange with pinkish blush tones. Works best in a gentle flame or encased.

5D0f6x.name: Exp. Poofs (Dense)
5D0f6x.description: A cadmium based orange works best in neutral flame.

2juNZY.name: Exp. Green Olive
2juNZY.description: This is an experimental green color, best worked gently in neutral to oxidizing flames or encased.

4X3b3N.name: Exp. Green Opal (Dense)
4X3b3N.description: This is a one of our new green opal colors, this is a dense batch.

0epFXm.name: Exp. Green Opal (unique)
0epFXm.description: A cadmium based green opal. This color works best in neutral to oxidizing flames or encased. This batch is slightly different than the original.

4KMD6y.name: Exp. Green Opal
4KMD6y.description: A cadmium based green opal. This color works best in neutral to oxidizing flames or encased.

4F8M5F.name: Exp. Light Blue Crimson
4F8M5F.description: Exp. Light Blue Crimson is a flame striking red with a light blue cobalt base.

24zb5E.name: Exp. Light Orange Rainbow
24zb5E.description: This color can produce a range of colors. Samples were struck in the kiln at 1125 for a short amount of time.

2zbTjr.name: Exp. Orange
2zbTjr.description: A vivid semi transparent cadmium based orange.

0T4TkN.name: Exp. Pink Grapefruit
0T4TkN.description: This is an experimental orange/pink cadmium color with similarities to orange opal.

40utga.name: Exp. Sonic Satin (Dense)
40utga.description: Our classic sonic with a satin twist.

4VQuZK.name: Exp. Transparent Green
4VQuZK.description: An experimental transparent green. Best worked in an oxidizing flame or encased.

4AycB7.name: Exp. Yellow Opal
4AycB7.description: Our newest batch of yellow opal rod. A vivid cadmium yellow with opal qualities best worked in a soft flame or encased.

4YzvUr.name: Globalt
4YzvUr.description: Global is a light cobalt color that glows a strong blue under UV light.

1JA9fT.name: Glopal
1JA9fT.description: Glopal is an easy to work and stable opal with a pink UV glow. Milky opaque appearance to unworked tube, with UV glow and opal quality allowing for more or less transparency depending on working conditions. Use a hotter flame for more transparent finish and less heat for a more opaque final product. A thin layer of clear adds durability for higher temp flames and sculpting.

6T0Hv3.name: Gold Purple
6T0Hv3.description: A gold based purple opal color. Color needs to be full worked for purple to strike. To avoid hazing on gold colors work in neutral to oxidizing flame or encase.

6edTAd.name: Grease Stain (Light Strike)
6edTAd.description: A yellowish color with light silver striking characteristics.

6UeR8Y.name: Green Energy (Light Strike)
6UeR8Y.description: This is a silver striking green, you can get a range of color from due to the striking properties.

4yt2Pt.name: Ice Water (UV)
4yt2Pt.description: This icy looking transparent glows pink under blacklight. A subtle hint of satin creates the ice water effect, resulting in a standalone clear transparent, or as a component in building layered colored tubes.

0JKNpc.name: Icy Blue Satin
0JKNpc.description: A icy blue with a satin shimmer and Uv reactive.

0sdn8e.name: Jungle Juice (variant)
0sdn8e.description: Jungle Juice is a rich dark green color with sparkle effect. Work gently and does not like deep encasements.

6R1Ece.name: Light Bright
6R1Ece.description: A clear that glows Pink/Orange under Uv light.

3KqMrC.name: Light Olive Oil
3KqMrC.description: A transparent yellow with slight opal affect.

3ZFRHe.name: Light Phoenix
3ZFRHe.description: Light Phoenix appears as a bright and rich ruby red. Very similar shade of red as standard Phoenix with a finished appearance closer to a traditional ruby red than an opal version. This is a perfect option when seeking a true transparent red that shines bright. Light Phoenix may appear transparent clear when working and before annealing. For a faster strike, raise kiln temperature as high as 1100.

057YXN.name: Light Russet
057YXN.description: A light brown with a slit tint of orange.

1knuzj.name: Mango
1knuzj.description: Mango is a vibrant translucent yellow orange in the pineapple juice family. Best worked in a gentle flame or encased.

1aL44u.name: Marina (Dense)
1aL44u.description: A denser batch than our classic Marina. Works best in neutral to oxidizing flames or encased.

3zsy6N.name: Marina
3zsy6N.description: Crisp aquatic blue reminiscent of a clear pond on a bright summer day, Marina is a copper based opal blue. Marina is similar to and in the family of Hydro. Like all opal type colors, it will appear more transparent when worked hotter and more milky when worked cooler. This new batch is slightly more transparent than the last batch.

5u6uML.name: Moist Raspberry (Unique)
5u6uML.description: This Moist Raspberry (Unique) Rod adds a vibrant pop of color to any project with its flame striking ruby red hue.

4d7TXA.name: Moist Raspberry
4d7TXA.description: A striking red, for best results flame strike then kiln strike.

0t7akf.name: Neo Opal (Dense)
0t7akf.description: A more dense version of our classic Neo Opal.

4vPWGU.name: Neo Opal
4vPWGU.description: Our classic Neo Opal Rod a translucent purple color with opal properties.

2AnAFH.name: Opal Light
2AnAFH.description: Opal Light is a lighter variety of Gopal with the same working characteristics. It has less opal strike which makes this a good color for overlay variations.

3x7PuA.name: Peach Opal Agate
3x7PuA.description: Lovely pinkish opal color that verges into an occasional amber.

02nm5A.name: Phoenix
02nm5A.description: Phoenix is juicy opal red color in the range of ruby with flashes of purple. Phoenix can produce a range of colors depending on strike.

2Dw6ax.name: Pineapple
2Dw6ax.description: Pineapple is a light yellow cadmium color worked best in a gentle neutral flame.

6MfG4g.name: Pumpkin
6MfG4g.description: A cadmium based color in similar shade to that of a pumpkin.

5KCXeD.name: Purple Rainbow (unique)
5KCXeD.description: A unique Striking purple rainbow. Wonderful silver based striking effect in this transparent purple. Work this color using flame chemistry in between neutral and oxidizing to maintain transparency. Strike using a slightly reducing flame or by leaving to soak in the kiln. Note that raising the temperature of the kiln is not always necessary for striking purple rainbow. 1080F for 3 - 4 hours

4JUnwK.name: Rainbow Opal
4JUnwK.description: The Rainbow Opal Rod adds a unique level of color and shimmer in the flame with its opalescent rainbow color shift. It works in both oxidizing and neutral atmospheres and contains a combination of opal and cfl to maximize color enhancement. Its striking effects add a vibrant decorative touch to any glass design.

257hBV.name: Rainbow Sample Pack V12
257hBV.description: These rainbow sample packs are darker/dense opal colors. They contain two rods of each color, Dark Phoenix, Russet Opal, Yellow Opal Satin, Green Opal, Blueberry Opal, and Dense Neo Opal.

6XD7Y5.name: Rainbow Sample Pack V13
6XD7Y5.description: These rainbow sample packs have 2 rods of each of the following colors Dark Phoenix, Exp. Orange, Dense Yellow Opal, Green Opal, Sonic, and Dense Neo Opal.

64cMrM.name: Rainbow Sample Pack V14
64cMrM.description: These rainbow sample packs are 1lb 2oz and have 2 rods of each color. Transitional Phoenix, Exp. Coral, Exp. Dense Yellow Opal, Green Opal, Marina, and Neo Opal.

0q0mXd.name: Rainbow Sample Pack V15
0q0mXd.description: We have another installation of our Rainbow Sample packs. This version is 1lb 1oz and includes two rods of each color - Transitional Phoenix, Dense Orange Opal (unique), Exp. Yellow Opal, Exp. Green Opal, Marina, and Neo Opal.

0J6wT4.name: Rose Quartz (Transparent)
0J6wT4.description: Transparent Rose Quartz is a lovely intense transparent pink with CFL reactivity. Under CFL it goes to a more intense electric hot pink.

0RgjHG.name: Rose Quartz
0RgjHG.description: Rose Quartz is a lovely transparent pink with slight opal effect. Under CFL it goes to a more intense pink.

5S909u.name: Russet Opal
5S909u.description: A light brown with opal qualities.

1TN2ze.name: Russet
1TN2ze.description: One of our newest browns added to the pallet. Works best in neutral flame.

2Adxds.name: Shifty Peach Light Opal Satin
2Adxds.description: Shifts from peach to pink under cfl, has a light opal and satin

63yUen.name: Smog
63yUen.description: A blue grey, with similarities to the hydro family with out the copper properties.

52wvgv.name: Sonic
52wvgv.description: Sonic is a rich blue opal. Similar in color to Dense Blue Cheese with an opal effect throughout.

3ZnbjT.name: Sparkle
3ZnbjT.description: Shiny metallic sparkle color. This is a great blingy sparkle rod in a classic gray metallic shade. Sparkle is a no-chrome metallic flake meaning it can be worked in any setting, surface or deep encasement.

2ebKg8.name: Striking Sample Pack V1
2ebKg8.description: This striking sample pack contains some of our striking colors. There are two rods of each color Light Moist Raspberry, Olive Oil Light, Grease Stain, Green Energy Light Strike, Transparent Gold Purple, and Cosmos.

04V7za.name: Transitional Cinnabar
04V7za.description: This is a semitransparent cadmium based orange, best worked in neutral to gentle oxidizing flames or encased.

3QdsVw.name: Transitional Mango
3QdsVw.description: Mango is a vibrant translucent yellow orange in the pineapple juice family. Best worked in a gentle flame or encased. This batch is more transparent then the last with a slight satin.

6adG8Q.name: Transitional Phoenix
6adG8Q.description: A red color with slight opal. This Phoenix is transitional due the amount of opal, it is in between Transparent Phoenix and Phoenix.

6B8xxz.name: Transitional Rose Quartz
6B8xxz.description: Rose Quartz is a lovely intense pink with CFL reactivity. Under CFL it goes to a more intense electric hot pink. Transitional refers to the opal content of the color and represents the mid point between Rose Quartz and Transparent Rose Quartz.

59XMC6.name: Transparent Coral
59XMC6.description: This is a cadmium based semi transparent orange.

1jqfeA.name: Transparent Gold Purple
1jqfeA.description: A transparent royal purple. The purple in this color is brought out by fully working it in cycles of letting it cool down and reheating similar to working an opal color.

5fgs9B.name: Transparent Gold Purple (Unique)
5fgs9B.description: A unique version of our transparent gold purple rod. This is unique due to the saturation of gold in the color and the hue before being melted. To bring out purple color must be fully worked.

6nye5x.name: Transparent Marina
6nye5x.description: A transparent non opal version of marina. This color works best in neutral to oxidizing flames, or encased.

5CYb42.name: Transparent Phoenix
5CYb42.description: Transparent Phoenix appears as a bright and rich ruby red. Very similar shade of red as standard Phoenix with a finished appearance closer to a traditional ruby red than an opal version. This is a perfect option when seeking a true transparent red that shines bright. Color can produce more of an opal effect when encased.

5DXDV9.name: Transparent Shifty Peach Opal
5DXDV9.description: A transparent version of our shifty peach. Changes from peach to bright pink under cfl light.

305yru.name: Transparent Shifty Sauce
305yru.description: A transparent color that shifts from yellow to pink under CFL.

2m5kDX.name: Transparent Yellow Opal
2m5kDX.description: A yellow with light opal, use neutral flame for best results.

3uneEK.name: White Satin
3uneEK.description: Hand pulled creamy opaque white with brilliant satin and pink under UV light. Satin colors really shine when encased.

3DJCJs.name: Wildberry (variant)
3DJCJs.description: This Wildberry variant has a slight satin effect, and stays opaque when worked. Best results in a neutral/oxidizing flame.

3693eK.name: Wildberry Satin
3693eK.description: Pleasing variety of Wildberry with a nice satin content. Mostly translucent color that will appear closer to opaque if kept thick, and more transparent if thinned or stretched.

5Sm0kR.name: Yoshi (Milky)
5Sm0kR.description: Milky Yoshi, a staple of the Greasy collection. Clean and nearly opaque with a strong CFL shift. This is B grade due to streaks.Easy to work. Preheat tubing slowly in kiln to avoid cracking.

0eEa67.name: Yoshi
0eEa67.description: Yoshi, a staple of the Greasy Glass collection. A vibrant green that shifts pink under CFL light.

4q5Nfu.name: Agua Azul
4q5Nfu.description: We've been testing out new and different materials to help maintain and even bring our prices down. This is your change to scoop some Experimental Agua Azul for a great price. Rods are First Quality, they work smooth and creamy. The rods are textured, but the texture goes away once heated. Working Tip: This is a user friendly color and can withstand long working times. As always, we suggest you use a neutral flame.

4mZBpA.name: Agua Mist
4mZBpA.description: We've been testing out new and different materials to help maintain and even bring our prices down. This is your change to scoop some Experimental Agua Mist for a great price. Rods are First Quality, they work smooth and creamy. The rods are textured, but the texture goes away once heated. Working Tip: This is a user friendly color and can withstand long working times. As always, we suggest you use a neutral flame.

5VMQ50.name: Amazon Lagoon
5VMQ50.description: We've been testing out new and different materials to help maintain and even bring our prices down. This is your change to scoop some Experimental Amazon Lagoon for a great price. Working Tip: Flame or kiln strike 1075F. Work neutral; reduce at end for metallic effects.

0Fj37Z.name: Aquatic Carnival
0Fj37Z.description: We've been testing out new and different materials to help maintain and even bring our prices down. This is your change to scoop some Experimental Aquatic Carnival for a great price. Expect the same great playful reaction on a slightly lighter base. We are loving this one. Working Tip: Flame or kiln strike 1075F. Work neutral; reduce at end for metallic effects.

4U2mv0.name: Argent Green
4U2mv0.description: It's Back!! This Test Lab color is back by popular demand. Previously, we had a Dark and a Light version. This time around, we made a shade in-between, hopefully you think it's just right. Working Tip: As always, we suggest you work in a neutral flame. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

2Xb6pE.name: Clear
2Xb6pE.description: Our clear frit is 100% crushed Simax, which is the clear we recommend to get optimal results from silver containing colors. This frit product is offered in 5 grade sizes.

2GR8x8.name: Cotton Candy
2GR8x8.description: Cotton Candy is a CFL shifter on a pastel base. This color is creamy and easy to work. Violet under natural light, the color will shift to a soft blue under CFL. Working Tip: Be sure not to get this color too hot when in a thin application as to not cook out the pastel base and turn it transparent. Work in a neutral flame. Blow outs work best with the pastel colors. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

6WPL70.name: Dandelion
6WPL70.description: Dandelion is a soft, sunny cadmium based yellow that comes alive when worked, striking to a warmer yellow than the rod. The seeded texture adds depth and character. Working Tip: Pre-heat in outer flame. Avoid rapid heating.

6NEP42.name: Double Dragon Hoodie
6NEP42.description: A soft and comfy unisex hoodie that fits all your hoodie needs. The Bella + Canvas fleece fabric makes it a great partner all year round. • 52% airlume combed and ring-spun cotton, 48% poly fleece* • Hood • Side seamed • Retail fit *Heather Colors: 60% airlume combed and ring-spun cotton, 40% poly fleece The male model is wearing size M. He's 6.0 feet (183 cm) tall, chest circumference 42.5" (108 cm), waist circumference 33.5" (85 cm). The female model is wearing a size M. She's 5.8 feet (178 cm) tall, chest circumference 34.6" (88 cm), waist circumference 27.1" (69 cm) and hip circumference 37.7" (96 cm). * Merch orders ship separately.

4TPCbr.name: Double Dragon Mug
4TPCbr.description: Whether you're drinking your morning coffee, your evening tea, or something in between – this mug's for you! This ceramic mug is sturdy and glossy with a vivid print that'll withstand the microwave and dishwasher. * Merch orders ship separately.

2ZTJhm.name: Dragon Tears
2ZTJhm.description: Dragon Tears is a transparent blue silver. This color is playful, while remaining transparent once worked. Working Tip: Work in a neutral flame and use a slightly reducing flame to bring the silver effects to the surface. Long kiln times will darken the effects, the base color will stay the same. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

5UfPsM.name: Eclipse
5UfPsM.description: We have been experimenting with different materials to find new ways to offer you lower prices. These are some of the batches of Eclipse. Expect the glass to work great, but the base color will be a bit bluer than our standard Eclipse offering. Working Tip: Work this color in a neutral flame.

4yFzYv.name: Ectoplasm
4yFzYv.description: Ectoplasm is a bright yellow-green with a touch of fuminess. This color can have different reactions in different flame atmospheres, achieving a range of effects. ﻿Working Tip: ﻿Work in a neutral flame and use a slightly reducing flame to bring the silver effects to the surface. You can also try running this color through multiple kiln cycles to activate the silver. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

1B4eJB.name: Experimental Silver #1
1B4eJB.description: We are excited to bring you a series of experimental silver colors that are variations of our Passion series. On the Singular to Triple Passion spectrum, Experimental Silver #1 is on the lighter side. Expect it to stay in the yellow range, with hints of light amber. If you like this one, please let us know so we can make it again!! Working Tip: Get this color white hot to erase the striking history. A variety of effects are achievable depending on how long you flame/kiln strike.

2Zp5Bw.name: Experimental Silver #2
2Zp5Bw.description: We are excited to bring you a series of experimental silver colors that are variations of our Passion series. On the Singular to Triple Passion spectrum, Experimental Silver #2 is more reactive than #1. Expect to push into the Amber range with some hints of Purple. If you like this one, please let us know so we can make it again!! Working Tip: Get this color white hot to erase the striking history. A variety of effects are achievable depending on how long you flame/kiln strike.

04t9Zj.name: Experimental Silver #3
04t9Zj.description: We are excited to bring you a series of experimental silver colors that are variations of our Passion series. Experimental Silver #3 is a reactive amber-purple color. Have fun, and if you like this one, please let us know so we can make it again!! Working Tip: Get this color white hot to erase the striking history. A variety of effects are achievable depending on how long you flame/kiln strike.

3hWerp.name: Experimental Silver #4
3hWerp.description: We are excited to bring you a series of experimental silver colors that are variations of our Passion series. Experimental Silver #4 is a reactive amber-purple color. Have fun, and if you like this one, please let us know so we can make it again!! Working Tip: Get this color white hot to erase the striking history. A variety of effects are achievable depending on how long you flame/kiln strike.

1s4SjA.name: Experimental Silver #5
1s4SjA.description: We are excited to bring you a series of experimental silver colors that are variations of our Passion series. Experimental Silver #5 is a reactive amber-purple color. Have fun, and if you like this one, please let us know so we can make it again!! Working Tip: Get this color white hot to erase the striking history. A variety of effects are achievable depending on how long you flame/kiln strike.

051LkB.name: Experimental Silver #6
051LkB.description: We are excited to bring you a series of experimental silver colors that are variations of our Passion series. Experimental Silver #6 is an extra rich reactive amber-purple color. Have fun, and if you like this one, please let us know so we can make it again!! Working Tip: Get this color white hot to erase the striking history. A variety of effects are achievable depending on how long you flame/kiln strike.

3kkGCz.name: Experimental Silver #7
3kkGCz.description: We are excited to bring you a series of experimental silver colors that are variations of our Passion series. Experimental Silver #6 is an extra rich reactive amber-purple color. Have fun, and if you like this one, please let us know so we can make it again!! Working Tip: Get this color white hot to erase the striking history. A variety of effects are achievable depending on how long you flame/kiln strike.

0mkZSZ.name: Logo Cuffed Beanie
0mkZSZ.description: A snug, form-fitting beanie with an embroidered GA logo. It's not only a great head-warming piece but will help keep you warm in your studio during winter. 100% Turbo Acrylic 12" in length Hypoallergenic Unisex style * Merch orders ship separately.

3U4QN5.name: Halo
3U4QN5.description: Halo is a beautiful transparent light yellow. This color is designed to stay yellow once kiln or flame struck. Working Tip: Flame or Kiln Strike

67g808.name: Light Marigold
67g808.description: This soft, transparent orange has a touch of subtle warmth. This is a less refined cadmium color, with a seeded look, creating a playful texture. Working Tip: Pre-heat in outer flame. Avoid rapid heating.

5JYgZb.name: Lite Sienna
5JYgZb.description: This is a lighter version than our standard color Sienna Brown. Working Tip: Work in neutral flame to avoid reduction

0y4gnU.name: Milk White
0y4gnU.description: This is an off shade of Sno White. Expect rods to be slightly off white with a hint of transparency. Working Tip: We recommend working in a neutral flame.

5ZMbCg.name: Pastel Voodoo
5ZMbCg.description: Pastel Voodoo is the same great CFL shifter you know and love on a pastel base. This color is creamy and easy to work. A soft dusty rose pink under natural light, the color will shift to a vibrant hot pink under CFL. Working Tip: Be sure not to get this color too hot when in a thin application as to not cook out the pastel base and turn it transparent. Work in a neutral flame. Blow outs work best with the pastel colors. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

4XpzLk.name: Peacock
4XpzLk.description: We've been testing out new and different materials to help maintain and even bring our prices down. This is your change to scoop some Experimental Peacock for a great price. Rods are First Quality, but there is some variance in overall saturation from rod to rod. When sleeved in clear, the rods can have a bit of transparency when pulled thin. Working Tip: This is a user friendly color and can withstand long working times. As always, we suggest you use a neutral flame.

6VjXuw.name: Ruby Strike
6VjXuw.description: This is a version of our old school Ruby Strike. A beautiful ruby that requires the kiln to strike. Rods will be transparent with a hint of red to light red in color. Working Tip: We recommend working in a neutral flame. Kiln strike.

5Fd3Xf.name: Sea Breeze
5Fd3Xf.description: Back by special request!! Sea Breeze is a beautiful blue-green. This color looks green in rod form and emits a beautiful blue around then edges when worked. Working Tip: As always, we suggest you work in a neutral flame. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

2mDKPk.name: Silver Potion
2mDKPk.description: We think you are going to love this one!! Potion, with a touch of silver. This color can have different reactions in different flame atmospheres, achieving a range of color effects. ﻿Working Tip: ﻿Work in a neutral flame and use a slightly reducing flame to bring the silver effects to the surface. You can also try running this color through multiple kiln cycles to activate the silver. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

3MKLQp.name: Silver Serum
3MKLQp.description: Silver Serum is here!! We debuted this color at our last Open House and it was met with rave reviews. What's not to like about Serum, with a touch of silver to make this CFL color even more playful. This color can have different reactions in different flame atmospheres, achieving a range of color effects. ﻿Working Tip: ﻿Work in a neutral flame and use a slightly reducing flame to bring the silver effects to the surface. You can also try running this color through multiple kiln cycles to activate the silver. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

61XCYm.name: Singular Passion
61XCYm.description: This color is a variation of Singular Passion, designed to stay in the yellow range and looks great layered over other colors. We have been experimenting with different silver color formulas to find new ways to have fun, reactive colors at a lower price. Let us know what you think!! Working Tip: Work this color in a neutral flame and treat it like any other Passion or Amber Purple color.

0xMstv.name: Sweet Heat
0xMstv.description: Sweet Heat is a smooth, buttery transparent orange. Lighter than Hot Sauce, Working Tip: Pre-heat in outer flame. Avoid rapid heating. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

5D8KGz.name: Tangie
5D8KGz.description: We are thrilled to introduce you all to Tangie! This color has been in the works for quite some time. You may have tried some Orange Shades test batches leading up to the development of this vibrant, easy to work semi-transparent orange. Working Tip: Pre-heat in outer flame. Avoid rapid heating. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

1mrC1n.name: Tequila NoRise
1mrC1n.description: This is a Tequila color, without the reds and pinks that are Tequila Sunrise. Expect amber and yellows from this one. Working Tip: We recommend working in a neutral flame. Kiln strike.

36vtXA.name: Unicorn Tears
36vtXA.description: Unicorn Tears is a beautiful pink-purple with a touch of silver for a fumey effect. Working Tip: Work in a neutral flame and use a slightly reducing flame to bring the silver effects to the surface. You can also try running this color through multiple kiln cycles to activate the silver. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

49qKKd.name: Wood Glue
49qKKd.description: ﻿This pastel based color is back by popular demand!! Wood Glue is a sibling of Glue Stick, with a little extra something to give it a great neutral color. Working Tip: Be sure not to get this color too hot when in a thin application as to not cook out the pastel base and turn it transparent. Blow outs work best of the pastel colors. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

0Y2Y5G.name: Clear Glow in the Dark
0Y2Y5G.description: Clear with glow in the dark frit. "Glow in the Dark! How fun is that?!!! This photo was taken in my bathroom with all the lights turned off. Veeery glowy! Shown here as spacers and encasing a black disc." – Janet Evans

0FH80r.name: Hydros
0FH80r.description: Summary: Reduction Color. Description: Hydros is a silver and copper glass creating an aquamarine color with a strong silver luster that maintains its pearlescence under encasement. To luster, work in a neutral flame, allow to cool for a few seconds, reheat far out in a large reducing flame.

2aM1JN.name: Ananke
2aM1JN.description: Summary: Reduction Color. Description: Ananke is a pure silver color that transmits a gold tone and develops a strong luster that maintains its pearlescence under encasement. Ananke is a reduction color. Work in a neutral flame, allow to cool for a few seconds, reheat far out in a large reducing flame.

0D9D6x.name: Arke 2
0D9D6x.description: Summary: Reducing. Description: Arke 2 is our updated formula that increased the silver and improved rod quality. Arke 2 is a transparent cobalt luster color that develops a variety of exterior metallic finishes and holds it’s luster under a clear encasement. It’s the lightest of our three cobalt silver glasses; Arke 2, Triton and Iris. Variations in flame chemistry, exposure time and temperature alter the color of the exterior luster.

1WsmQ6.name: Atlas 2
1WsmQ6.description: Summary: Extra Strength Striking Glass. Description: Atlas 2 is formulated in our updated color base with the same nucleation system as our other striking colors. Atlas 2 is a highly saturated with silver as the only colorant. It can produce a range of colors both transparent and opaque, including ambers, purples, blues, and greens. It works well in both surface and encased applications. Atlas 2 is easy to strike using the reset/cool/warm sequence. It is very responsive to varied thermal history, allowing the development of many different colors on the same piece. Our benchmark times for surface application are Reset/30 seconds cool/30 seconds strike. A clear encasement layer adds about 15 seconds to the cooling and striking times. Specific times and color outcomes will vary depending on several factors.

2JnphH.name: Oracle Celadon Pastel
2JnphH.description: Summary: Technical. Description: Oracle Celadon Pastel is made in our smooth melting Oracle White 2 base. The Oracle project gives 104 flame workers the option to use responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses in their work. All of our Oracle glasses are made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium.

4Wu64a.name: Oracle Lapis
4Wu64a.description: Summary: Technical. Description: Oracle Lapis is a rich cobalt blue opaque made in our smooth melting Oracle White 2 base glass. The Oracle project gives 104 flame workers the option to use responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses in their work. All of our Oracle glasses are made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium.

67pUV8.name: Oracle ExtraBlack
67pUV8.description: Summary: Oracle ExtraBlack; for best results, use a slightly oxidizing flame and avoid overheating.. Description: Oracle ExtraBlack has smooth working characteristics, reads dark even when pulled thin, and does not spread excessively. Oracle ExtraBlack is made in USA without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium. The goal of the Oracle project create is to create American made, low-toxicity, essential glass colors for the flame. We will be producing colors free from antimony, arsenic, cadmium, chromium, lead and selenium. Oracle Black, Oracle White2, Rhea, Eros, Zephyr and Oracle ExtraBlack give 104 flame workers the option to use responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses in their work.

66zCKg.name: Oracle White 2
66zCKg.description: Oracle White 2 is smoother melting than the original. It is our house white that we use in our murrini. The Oracle project gives 104 flame workers the option to use responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses in their work. All of our Oracle glasses are made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium.

5BP8WV.name: Oracle Pink Pastel
5BP8WV.description: Summary: Technical. Description: Oracle Pink Pastel is a nearly opaque glass that requires no special treatment to develop its smooth and consistent soft pink tone. The Oracle project gives 104 flame workers the option to use responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses in their work. All of our Oracle glasses are made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium.

3QzHXm.name: Elpis 2
3QzHXm.description: Summary: Reducing Glass. Description: Elpis 2 is made in our updated color base resulting in cleaner colors, smoother working characteristics and improved viscosity curves. Elpis 2 is a chrome-free green reducing glass that transmits a spring green color and is resistant to over reducing. Based on test batch PX-772.

59pmCS.name: Oracle Opal 2
59pmCS.description: Summary: Technical Opal. Description: Oracle Opal 2 is a cleaner brighter formula than Oracle Opal. Oracle Opal 2 is a striking glass that produces a range of misty opal tones. It easily resets to crystal clear, initiating the striking process. After resetting, Oracle Opal 2 will cool to a faint translucent opalescence. Further exposure to flame temperatures around 1000°F will cause more extensive opacification. For Best Results: Higher temperatures and longer annealing times can initiate further striking of the opal. Encasing the Opal will also add heat and time so adjust your annealing accordingly or plan on having more opacity. The Bead: Zephyr core, layer of Oracle Opal 2, encased in Zephyr, with Oracle Opal 2 scroll-work The Oracle Project – responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium. Balancing viscosity curves, opacity, tonality, surface tension, and thermal shock resistance, to create glass that is a pleasure to work with in the flame.

5vctsk.name: Eros
5vctsk.description: Summary: Technical Glass. Description: Eros, our gold-pink. Based on test batch HWP-791 and Rhea Light. Avoid overheating to maintain color. The Lighter Bead: is Eros sandwiched between layers of Zephyr with Eros scroll work. The Darker Bead: a core of Eros encased in Zephyr with Eros scroll work.

2FKF05.name: Hyperborea
2FKF05.description: Summary: Reducing Glass. Description: Hyperborea has a rich violet and red color transmission and easily develops a strong silver luster when reduced. It works well both in surface applications and under encasement. The color is saturated and may present best over a core of clear glass, as pictured. A replacement to Boreas, Hyperborea is made in our updated color base resulting in cleaner colors, smoother working characteristics and improved viscosity curves. Based off of the BE test batches.

4zzNMu.name: Okeanos 2
4zzNMu.description: Summary: Dual; Strike or Reduce. Description: Okeanos 2 is a blue striking and reducing color. Reformulated with the same nucleation system as Terra 3 and Ekho 2, it strikes to a range of blues, greens, purples and amber. It works well on the surface or encased. Super-heating can cause phase separation, resulting in webbing. Okeanos 2 is capable of developing a subtle luster and retaining that luster under clear encasement. Okeanos 2 is easy to strike using the reset/cool/warm sequence. Our benchmark times for surface application are Reset/30 seconds, cool/30 seconds, strike. Specific times and color outcomes vary depending on several factors.

45tybQ.name: Ekho 2
45tybQ.description: Summary: Striking and Reducing. Description: Ekho2 is a dual color, capable of both reducing and striking. It works best if you choose one technique or the other. Ekho2 is a reformulated version of Ekho. The nucleation system used in Skylla and Skiron has been added, resulting in a glass that is easier to strike. Ekho2 can be used as a surface luster, an encased pearlescent luster, struck on the surface, or struck under a thin encasement layer. The cooling and warming portions of the striking sequence for this glass are both approximately 45 seconds for the bead size and shape pictured. Specific times may vary depending on several factors. For best results in a striking application, apply a thin layer of clear glass to encase, then reset the Ekho2, cool, and strike the color through the clear. For detailed instructions, see our SnapGuide tutorial .

2YL1f5.name: Lotis
2YL1f5.description: Summary: Gold Pink.. Description: A pink version of Rhea. A lead free gold pink that plays well with silver colors and survives a reduction flame without discolorations. From test batch RO-682

3LrmD3.name: Phoebe
3LrmD3.description: Summary: Phoebe is a luster glass saturated with silver. Based on the 2017 test batch ZL-689.. Description: Phoebe is a luster glass saturated with silver. Based on the 2017 test batch ZL-689. See Jed’s tutorial on How to Make a Hot Pink Bead with Rhea, Phoebe and Zephyr.

6ETv7f.name: Oracle Black
6ETv7f.description: Summary: Oracle-Black; Neutral with striking colors, reactive with lusters. Kiln-strikes to final opacity and tonality.. Description: Oracle-Black made in typical Double Helix fashion; with unconventional approaches to glass chemistry using low toxicity ingredients. Oracle-Black has smooth working characteristics, reads “darker” than some existing black glasses, does not spread excessively, and can be worked very hot without boiling. It is made in USA without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium. Rods are dark blue but strike to black during the annealing cycle. Stays neutral with striking colors but reacts to luster colors. For maximum opacity, particularly in thin applications, briefly cool the bead then lightly flame strike (30 seconds) before annealing for 2 hours or more at 950F. The Oracle projec t is an extension of what we’ve already done with Aether, Zephyr and Rhea; create low-toxicity, essential glass colors for the flame. We will be producing colors free from antimony, arsenic, cadmium, chromium, lead and selenium. Oracle-Black, Oracle-White (coming in 2018), Rhea, and Zephyr give 104 flame workers the option to use responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses in their work. Stunning. Buttery smooth to work, and the silver reactions are outstanding. Use with silver foil, or silver laden frit for absolutely fantastic effects.

4fheHL.name: Skiron
4fheHL.description: Summary: Skiron is our new silver-striking, rainbow glass.. Description: Skiron is our new, sliver-striking, rainbow glass. A major improvement over Luna 3 and Khaos, it resists over striking to khaki. Skiron works best when reset, cooled, and struck. Cooling and striking times will vary based on bead size, flame temperature, and other factors but general guidelines are; Surface applications: reset, cool for 30 seconds, strike for 30-45 seconds. Encased applications: encase, reset, cool for 45 seconds, strike for 45-60 seconds. The cooling cycle is an important factor in repeatable end results. Shorter than recommended cooling times typically yield white and purple, while longer cooling times can yield dark Amber with blue tints. Somewhere in between lies the ideal cooling/striking timing for your application and set up. Learn More View Jed’s tutorial on How to Make a Skiron and Aether Bead.

0NfSC3.name: Iris
0NfSC3.description: Iris is the production version of the popular test batch AX-605. The A was for Arke and the X was for 10 times the strength! Though designed specifically for exterior applications, the silver portion of the luster will hold up under encasement. This reduction color can yield a multicolored metallic iridescent luster. Here’s a short video of the process. In our experience, a brush reduction flame produces the best results. Tips from Jed: It does require particular flame settings, and bead heat and reduction duration are more critical. My specific timings work for my specific set up. It is going to vary from person to person. Here is my process. 1) Shape bead 2) Allow bead to cool for 20 seconds. 3) Adjust flame so candles are stretched 2mm from neutral. 4) Pass bead through flame, candles should touch bead and deflect yellow flame around the edges. 1.5 seconds duration for each pass. 5) Allow bead to cool 5 seconds between passes. 6) Repeat pass-through and cooling cycle 5-15 times. 7) Anneal.

0emKjR.name: Hyperion Light
0emKjR.description: Summary: For best results, follow the reset and cooling process for Striking Colors, then reduce.. Description: A lighter version of Hyperion. Hyperion is a relative of Clio and our CX test series. A strong reduction color that is designed to strike automatically during the bead making process to medium amber. Encasing the light reduction in clear results in a purple pearlescent luster. For best results, follow the reset and cooling process for Striking Colors, then reduce.

1CnMGZ.name: Hyperion
1CnMGZ.description: Summary: For best results, follow the reset and cooling process for Striking Colors, then reduce.. Description: Hyperion is a relative of Clio and our CX test series. A strong reduction color that is designed to strike automatically during the bead making process to medium amber. Encasing the light reduction in clear results in a purple pearlescent luster. For best results, follow the reset and cooling process for Striking Colors, then reduce.

17bNwy.name: Ossa
17bNwy.description: Summary: Speckled Luster. Description: Ossa is the first in our new speckled color family. Based on the popular “speckled luster” test batches OP-434 and OP-507. Ossa is a rich purple lustering glass with thousands of refractive inclusions dispersed throughout each rod. When exposed on the surface, Ossa can be left as a purple speckled glass, or it can be reduced to develop a variety of luster effects. Using variations in flame chemistry, Ossa can produce a solid silver metallic layer, or a multicolored iridescence. When reduced and encased, the inclusions in Ossa produce a textured mother-of-pearl effect reminiscent of some dichroic coatings.

3AyYg5.name: Notos
3AyYg5.description: Summary: Notos is a silver saturated super-luster with a subtle blue-grey-green tone.. Description: Notos is a silver saturated super-luster with a subtle blue-grey-green tone. This color is an enhanced, stronger lustering version of OK-455, which proved very popular at the 2011 ISGB Gathering. Reduce and encase with Zephyr for cool blue tones, and with Aether for soft green tones. Repeated, gentle reduction can yield pink iridescent lusters.

3D9pBS.name: Kalypso
3D9pBS.description: Summary: Striking and reducing. Description: Kalypso is more intense and saturated version of Clio. It’s a color-shifting, reset-reduce glass, that transmits ambers and reds with the reds being more visible under incandescent and sunlight. It develops a strong silver luster and maintains its pearlescence under encasement. Reset-Reduce colors need to be reset in a neutral flame before following the reducing process. See our guide on how to reset. See our Phaeton Tutorial for the best techniques to use with Clio. Based of of test batches NE-323, KA-356 and KA-357. WONDERFUL….. I want to cry while this glass.Color transitions making me crazy.And the result is excellent. TIDES OF CREATION This is easily my favorite glass. It is so easy to get the most amazing colors out of this glass. Simply stunning! I LOVE THIS COLOR I love pink and purple especially but this color is very easy to strike and work with. I am so glad it exists. Please keep up the outstanding work and coming up with such amazing colors for us.

72844m.name: Aurae Light
72844m.description: Summary: Reduction Color. Description: Aurae light has the same silver-reduction strength as regular Aurae with a pink base color. Variations in the reduction process create mirrored, iridescent or satin textured lusters. If encased, the luster results in a pearlescent effect. Work in a neutral flame. Cool until the glass is no longer glowing. Expose the glass to a reduction flame, while keeping it from getting hot. Brief (5-10 seconds) and repeated exposures produces the best results. For the satin textured luster, work in the tip of a larger reduction flame, let cool and then briefly reduce again until a subtle texture begins to form. See our How To section for more detailed working information and tips on using our reduction colors. What are Odd Lots (Light, Dark, Odd) An Odd Lot is a batch of a regular stock color that did not pass its color matching test. If it was lighter than the standard, it’s labeled light. Darker, labeled Dark. For any other non color matching reason, it’s labeled Odd. Therfore, one batch of Light to another will not necessarily be the same. Some could be slightly lighter than the standard and others much lighter. A picture of the current batch of Light is in the gallery for your reference. MY ALL TIME GO TO FOR SCROLLWORK. only glass I don’t have to reduce to bring up the luster (for times I don’t want a lot of fuming), but if reduced its deep and lots of pink highlights. AURAE LIGHT Love, love, love this version. Please keep making it. Colleen ARTIST I love all 3 version of Aurae! Keep them coming.

6kaXZs.name: Aurae
6kaXZs.description: Summary: Reduction Color. Description: Aurae is a light purple, silver-reduction glass. Variations in the reduction process create mirrored, iridescent or satin textured lusters. If encased, the luster results in a pearlescent effect. Work in a neutral flame. Cool until the glass is no longer glowing. Expose the glass to a reduction flame, while keeping it from getting hot. Brief (5-10 seconds) and repeated exposures produces the best results. For the satin textured luster, work in the tip of a larger reduction flame, let cool and then briefly reduce again until a subtle texture begins to form. See our How To section for more detailed working information and tips on using our reduction colors. ONE OF MY FAVS Love it! Really love the golden mirror-like finish it produces…perfectly lovely. ARTIST I LOVE all 3 versions of this glass, wonderful reactions and easy to use. Keep them coming! WONDERFUL COLOR wonderful perfect color 5 star company & customer service

1CweW3.name: Triton
1CweW3.description: Summary: Reduction Color. Description: Triton is an extra strength silver luster color on a cobalt blue base. The result of test batches K-65, K-102, and K-108 It can produce a satin iridescence, swirls of multi-colored silver and retain its luster under clear. Work in a neutral flame, allow to cool for a few seconds, reheat far out in a large reducing flame. For the multi-colored satin effect work in the tip of a larger reduction flame, let cool and then briefly reduce again. BEAUTIFUL METALLIC COLOR Triton is a shade I use on a regular basis. It’s absolutely beautiful! Can’t go wrong with Triton 🙂 OUT STANDING COLOR This is the best, easy to decorate with, striking beautiful color. If this glass isn’t in your studio, it needs to be…… My favourite Double Helix glass frit, easy to reduce, love it on a black or dark blue back.

6s93B0.name: Psyche
6s93B0.description: Summary: Reduction Color. Description: Psyche is strong silver reduction glass in a dark purple base. Depending on the reduction process, Psyche can produce a mirrored or rainbow oil slick appearance. If encased, the luster results in a pearlescent effect. Work in a neutral flame. Cool until the glass is no longer glowing. Expose the glass to a reduction flame, while keeping it from getting hot. Brief (5-10 seconds) and repeated exposures produces the best results. See our How To section for more detailed working information and tips on using our reduction colors. ONE OF MY FAVORITE DH COLORS I can pull fabulous pearlescent colors from this glass. My customers love it. Easy to work with everytime. MY FAVORITE SILVER GLASS If DH stops making it I don’t want to go on living. Beautiful when encased. GREAT COLOR! Psyche is one of my favorite DH glass colors. It can reduce to a gorgeous mirror shine and encased, I get the most amazing purple, pink, blue & green with a really lovely mother of pearl shine. Love this glass! A timeless part of my glassworking kit. Offers a stunning range of colors from a single gather’s application if teased into reduction in stages. I’ll be sad if they ever discontinue this one–it helped me make some of the pieces that inspired me to stick with lampwork.

4fWbQq.name: Oracle-804.AuOpl
4fWbQq.description: Summary: Pink fast opal. Description: Oracle-804.AuOpl , a pink fast opal. This opal is a striking glass that produces a range of misty opal pink tones. It easily resets to crystal clear, initiating the striking process. After resetting, it will cool to a faint translucent opalescence. This opal is “fast” compared to our regular oracle opal, and it will develop substantial opacity when annealed at 920F. For Best Results: Reset the Opal before annealing at 920°F for up to two hours. A translucent, opalescent strike will occur at these annealing temperatures. Higher temperatures and longer annealing times will initiate further striking of the opal. Encasing the Opal will also add heat and time so adjust your annealing accordingly or plan on having more opacity. The Beads: the horizontal bead is a wigwag bead with Oracle-802.AuOpl and Zephyr. The vertical bead is a wigwag of Zephyr and cane of 802.AuOpl encased in Zephyr.

5ERgcM.name: Oracle-803.AuOpl
5ERgcM.description: Summary: purple slow opal, sold @ $60/pound. Description: Oracle-803.AuOpl , a purple slow opal. This opal is a striking glass that produces a range of misty opal pink tones. It easily resets to transparent pale purple. After resetting, it will cool to a faint translucent opalescence. This opal is “slow” compared to our regular oracle opal, and it may require very gentle flame striking or longer annealing times or higher annealing temperatures to develop substantial opacity. For Best Results: Reset the Opal before annealing at 920°F for two hours or more. A translucent, opalescent strike can occur at annealing temperatures above 920F. Higher temperatures and longer annealing times will initiate further striking of the opal. The opal strike may also be initiated by resetting, cooling, and striking in a very cool flame before annealing. The Bead: is a wigwag bead with Oracle-803.AuOpl+Zephyr cane and Zephyr encasement dots.

3guJLa.name: Oracle-802.AuOpl
3guJLa.description: Summary: Pink fast opal. Description: Oracle-802.AuOpl , a pink fast opal. This opal is a striking glass that produces a range of misty opal pink tones. It easily resets to crystal clear, initiating the striking process. After resetting, it will cool to a faint translucent opalescence. This opal is “fast” compared to our regular oracle opal, and it will develop substantial opacity when annealed at 920F. For Best Results: Reset the Opal before annealing at 920°F for up to two hours. A translucent, opalescent strike will occur at these annealing temperatures. Higher temperatures and longer annealing times will initiate further striking of the opal. Encasing the Opal will also add heat and time so adjust your annealing accordingly or plan on having more opacity. The Bead: is a wigwag bead with Oracle-802.AuOpl and Zephyr.

54Ek3t.name: Oracle-792.yopl
54Ek3t.description: Summary: Yellow Opal. Description: Oracle-792yopl , our Oracle Opal with a hint of yellow. Our opal is a striking glass that produces a range of misty opal tones. It easily resets to crystal clear, initiating the striking process. After resetting, it will cool to a faint translucent opalescence. Further exposure to flame temperatures around 1000°F will cause more extensive opacification. For Best Results: If you’d like to retain the color effect as-is when you’re done, anneal cool at about 920°F for up to two hours. Higher temperatures and longer annealing times will initiate further striking of the opal. Encasing the Opal will also add heat and time so adjust your annealing accordingly or plan on having more opacity. The Bead: is a wigwag bead with Oracle-792.yopl and Zephyr.

4DCK86.name: Oracle-789.blopl
4DCK86.description: Summary: Blue Opal, $12.50/quarter pound. Description: Oracle-789.blopl , our Oracle Opal with a blue tint. Our opal is a striking glass that produces a range of misty opal tones. It easily resets to crystal clear, initiating the striking process. After resetting, it will cool to a faint translucent opalescence. Further exposure to flame temperatures around 1000°F will cause more extensive opacification. 46Xzkj.name: Oracle-790.pkopl
46Xzkj.description: Summary: Pink Opal. Description: Oracle-790.pkopl . Our opal is a striking glass that produces a range of misty opal tones. 3U8eZk.name: Oracle-779.vtrn
3U8eZk.description: Summary: Transparent violet-purple, neutral glass.. Description: Oracle-779.vtrn is a transparent violet-purple glass. It is a neutral glass and has with no special working requirements. The Oracle Project – responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium. Balancing viscosity curves, opacity, tonality, surface tension, and thermal shock resistance, to create glass that is a pleasure to work with in the flame. The Oracle Project Test Batches – offered direct from the glassmaker to the artisan. Labeled with batch date and formula number, with a suffix to indicate glass family type example, 740.opl. I have thoroughly enjoyed researching, developing, batching, testing, and using these colors, and it is my sincere hope that these glasses enhance your flameworking experience. -Jed at Double Helix Glassworks

2ktJ5X.name: Oracle-754.opl
2ktJ5X.description: Summary: Slow Opal. Description: 754.opl is a slow opal that strikes in the flame and kiln. When reset it is crystal clear and when fully struck it’s milky opaque white. Areas that have started to opacify in the flame will continue to opacify in the annealer. Striking temperatures are lower than that of our silver glasses. Working notes: This slow opal stays mostly reset during many beadmaking operations, and will strike to a misty-opal during annealing. I anneal this color at 975°F for up to five hours for misty-opal beads, depending on size, encasement, and other factors. Your kiln is probably different than mine. Test beads are recommended. -Jed at Double Helix Glassworks

1Jch9C.name: Oracle-719.pst
1Jch9C.description: Summary: Pastel glass. Description: 719.pst a pastel glass, neutral-white with a hint of pink. The pale pink undertone develops during heating and cooling cycles. Sold at $10/quarter. The Oracle Project – responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium. Balancing viscosity curves, opacity, tonality, surface tension, and thermal shock resistance, to create glass that is a pleasure to work with in the flame. I have thoroughly enjoyed researching, developing, batching, testing, and using these colors, and it is my sincere hope that these glasses enhance your flameworking experience. -Jed at Double Helix Glassworks

2Kwb0B.name: Oracle-780.vopl
2Kwb0B.description: Summary: Slow Violet Opal. Description: 780.vopl is a violet tinted slow opal that opacifies in the flame and kiln. When reset, the glass is transparent violet, and when fully struck the glass is an opaque lavender color. Areas that have started to opacify in the flame will continue to opacify in the annealer. Striking temperatures are lower than that of our silver glasses. Working notes: This slow opal stays mostly reset during many beadmaking operations, and can strike to a misty-opal or opaque lavender color during annealing. I anneal this color at 975°F for up to five hours for semi-opaque beads, depending on size, encasement, and other factors. Your kiln is probably different than mine. Test beads are recommended. -Jed at Double Helix Glassworks

5r8ym3.name: Oracle-752.opl
5r8ym3.description: Summary: Was sold at $30/pound.. Description: 752.opl – An opal glass that strikes in the flame and kiln. Compared to the 740/743.opl it is slower striking, and more translucent after annealing. 752.opl can be worked hot and fast in the torch flame. Working notes: -To retain the transparent opal effect, limit kiln temperature and annealing time. I use 920F for up to two hours for misty-opal beads. Clear encasement seems to accelerate opacification in the annealer. Kilns vary in the amount of heat at the beads’ location vs the displayed temperature. Your kiln is probably different than mine. Test beads are recommended. -A Reset/Cooling/Striking cycle can be used in the flame to alter the appearance of the opal effect. An encased bead that has been reset, air-cooled for 45 seconds, then very gently struck for 45 seconds seems to maintain the opalescent effect better than a bead annealed directing after resetting. The 752.opl’s reset and striking temperatures are lower than that of silver glasses. When reset, the glass is crystal clear, and when fully struck the glass is a milky opaque white. Variable opacity can be produced by controlling the thermal history of the workpiece. The Oracle Project – responsibly manufactured, low toxicity glasses made in the USA, without Antimony, Arsenic, Cadmium, Chromium, Lead, Nickel, or Selenium. Balancing viscosity curves, opacity, tonality, surface tension, and thermal shock resistance, to create glass that is a pleasure to work with in the flame. The Oracle Project Test Batches – offered direct from the glassmaker to the artisan in small batches, sold by the pound, wrapped in paper. 0bbZUC.name: Oracle-743.opl
0bbZUC.description: Summary: was sold at $30/pound. Description: 743.opl : An opal glass that strikes in the flame and kiln. With a (relatively) high resistance to thermal shock, 743.opl can be worked hot and fast in the torch flame. It is significantly stiffer than a typical opaque white glass, making it suitable for sculptural work, bead cores, and stringers. Working notes: -743.opl works the same as 740.opl -To retain the transparent opal effect, reset before annealing and limit kiln temperature and annealing time. I use 930F for less than an hour for misty-opal beads. -743.opl can be used as a core in place of opaque white glasses. For maximum opacity, anneal at 950F for 2 hours of more. Clear encasement seems to accelerate opacification in the annealer. The 743.opl’s reset and striking temperatures are lower than that of silver glasses. When reset, the glass is crystal clear, and when fully struck the glass is opaque white. Variable opacity can be produced by controlling the thermal history of the workpiece. 3eZ4e2.name: Oracle-750.pst
3eZ4e2.description: Summary: 750.pst – a pastel glass, cream tonality. Avoid overheating to prevent “fizz”.. Description: 750.pst – a pastel glass, neutral-yellow tonality. Sold at $30/pound. Working notes: Avoid overheating to prevent “fizz”. Opacity can increase with extended annealing, with color outcomes ranging from slightly translucent cream to a warm almost-White. Opacity may increase during annealing, resulting in a lighter finished color outcome. 4T65T4.description: Summary: 742.pst – a pastel glass, light pink tonality.. Description: 742.pst – a pastel glass, light pink tonality. $30/pound Working notes: Moderately translucent character in thin applications, pale pink opaque in thicker applications. 3PumMu.name: Acid Yellow Crayon
3PumMu.description: The new batches of Acid Yellow Crayon are the most dense yet! We are pushing this color's boundaries, making it as dense as possible, while keeping it an acidic lemony yellow. If you want a more traditional yellow, try Yellow Crayon. Working Tip: Pre-heat in outer flame. Avoid rapid heating Artist Description by Mike Shelbo: "This very bright opaque yellow will stay true when drawn down to smaller cane sizes and will not transmit light unless the application of color is thinner than 2mm. This color works great in the neutral flame region and can handle all flame atmospheres for short amounts of time. Do not use a highly reducing flame or a very sharp hot flame without quick movement of the color; this will avoid any possibility of minor boil spots. The vibrancy of Acid Yellow Crayon is a wonderful backing to many Glass Alchemy transparent colors, also a very complimentary color to the other opaques, and desirable for murine applications as well. Encasement in clear is not necessary but can be used to increase yield on size of solid or blown work and allow for more intense working conditions." - Mike Shelbo

3zAtpf.name: Agua Azul
3zAtpf.description: Agua Azul, 446 is hailed by many as the best boro color ever. It looks great on its own, compliments or contrasts nearly all colors in the Glass Alchemy palette, and works great in encasement applications. These features and many more have allowed Agua Azul, 446 to become one of the finest opaques in the borosilicate world. Working Tip: Work this color in a neutral flame. Garage at 975° F, Anneal at 1050° F. Artist Description by Mike Shelbo: "This opaque aqua blue works great and has never given me any problems. I know that it is one of the most popular Glass Alchemy colors and the reason is because no matter which way you work it, the results are fantastic. I use it for murrine, solid sculpture, blown work on clear tubing or coil potted and with or without encasement in clear. Agua Azul holds its color as it is drawn out into stringers and is applied smoothly and works creamy. When blown extremely thin you can see slight translucent qualities and minuscule air bubbles, but this only shows when not encased and blown thinner than 1mm. Complimenting and contrasting a wide array of Glass Alchemy colors, Agua Azul is a mandatory part of my palette and has been since I first used it long ago." - Mike Shelbo

5V6T0R.name: Agua Azul
5V6T0R.description: We've been testing out new and different materials to help maintain and even bring our prices down. This is your change to scoop some Experimental Agua Azul for a great price. Rods are First Quality, they work smooth and creamy. The rods are textured, but the texture goes away once heated. Working Tip: This is a user friendly color and can withstand long working times. As always, we suggest you use a neutral flame.

2yzmR3.name: Agua Mist
2yzmR3.description: Agua Mist, 443 is a smooth and creamy blue-green that falls between Agua Azul and Alchemy Mint. This color rounds out the water fade and has similar working properties to Agua Azul. This color looks great on its own and compliments or contrasts nearly all colors in the Glass Alchemy palette. Working Tip: Work this color in a neutral flame. Garage at 975° F, Anneal at 1050° F. Artist Description by Mike Shelbo: "This opaque color is the in between shade of GA Alchemy Mint and GA Agua Azul. It is a wonderful blend that is similar to the color of conventional toothpaste. It handles really well in all flame atmospheres and can be worked very easily with or without encasement. Agua Mist melts smooth and creamy, so it works like a dream. Great for hollow or solid work and is light when drawn out to a stringer but still holds its color well." - Mike Shelbo

1Q07Jr.name: Agua Mist
1Q07Jr.description: We've been testing out new and different materials to help maintain and even bring our prices down. This is your change to scoop some Experimental Agua Mist for a great price. Rods are First Quality, they work smooth and creamy. The rods are textured, but the texture goes away once heated. Working Tip: This is a user friendly color and can withstand long working times. As always, we suggest you use a neutral flame.

27a7Hh.name: Alchemy Mint
27a7Hh.description: Alchemy Mint, 441 is an opaque celadon green that works well in fades, backgrounds to pop other colors or as an off white, especially in stringer applications. Working Tip: Work this color in a neutral flame. Garage at 975° F, Anneal at 1050° F. Artist Description by Mike Shelbo: "I work this color unencased and it works creamy and smooth in a variety of flame settings. Quick heats with a sharp premix flame to add, melt or cut-in detail work does not bother the surface of this color. This is a beautiful opal that will lend well to blown work and contrasts with darker colors. If blown thin enough, you will see a milky opalescent finish that is easiest to achieve by placing Mint in between two layers of clear before blowing out." - Mike Shelbo

0pvJ9S.name: Amazon Bronze
0pvJ9S.description: Henry designed this color for Susan to look like a Japanese ceramic glaze. Amazon Bronze is loaded with metals, which gives this color a very fun nature. Working Tip: Flame or kiln strike 1075F. Work neutral; reduce at end for metallic effects. Artist Description by Mike Shelbo: "The potential for variations of finishes is the best part about Amazon Bronze. I usually work the glass in the center of the distance between my torch tip and the end of the flame (the neutral flame zone), leaving me with a deep reddish brown. Then when the piece is completed and ready to put away I will increase propane in the flame and flash the piece in and out of the fire to bring the metallic reduction to the surface. This has yielded metallic colors ranging from a shiny copper penny to a beautiful rainbow iridescence. You can also repeatedly kiln your finished piece at 1040F to 1100F to achieve a metallic effect, leaving a slight luster finish of blues and purples and sometimes cream and green on top of your underlying dense browns and reds. Amazon Bronze looks awesome without being encased or underneath clear or other transparent colors." - Mike Shelbo

3BhUUd.name: Amazon Lagoon
3BhUUd.description: After first introducing information on how to strike silver colors and create metallic finishes, such as using a neutral flame and monitoring time/temperature relationships, we started to hear that some people missed the "surprise" of opening their kiln door. For all of you that fit into this category, we created Amazon Lagoon, 587. This color was designed to put the "surprise" back into working silver borosilicate colors. Every piece will be beautiful, every piece will be different. Working Tip: Work in neutral flame and have fun, this one is loaded with silver! Artist Description by Mike Shelbo: "Amazon Lagoon is a very deep cobalt base glass packed with tons of silver. Encasement of the rod in clear will result in trapping pearlescent greens and blues and some golden oranges and cream yellows. Depending on working time and whether the piece is solid or blown, you will see a range of finishes and shifting of colors. In a neutral working atmosphere the silver will come to the surface when not encased in clear. Color ranging from dark blue to yellow green pastel will sometimes have streaks of cool colors on the surface. When your piece is done you can reduce lightly and watch the metallic finish emerge in golds, silvers, greens, bronzes and blues depending on color layer thickness and amount of reduction given." - Mike Shelbo

2R5fap.name: Amazon Lagoon
2R5fap.description: We've been testing out new and different materials to help maintain and even bring our prices down. This is your change to scoop some Experimental Amazon Lagoon for a great price. Working Tip: Flame or kiln strike 1075F. Work neutral; reduce at end for metallic effects.

6hYpxY.name: Amazon Night
6hYpxY.description: The year was 2001 and it was Henry's birthday. He had never given himself a birthday present so he figured it was time to change that. Four days later on October the 9th Amazon Night, 987 was born. His baby is a beautiful green with silver that produces amazing strikes and silver lusters. This color is also our preferred method for testing for a neutral flame. Also available in frit, this color is a must have for every studio! Working Tip: Flame or kiln strike at 1075°F. Work neutral; reduce at end for metallic effects. Artist Description by Mike Shelbo: "The base glass for Amazon Night is a translucent dark green and it is fully packed with silver and other metals. I love to encase this color with clear on a piece that will be worked for a couple hours. Reheating the area of Amazon Night in different ways (ex: sharp intense spot heat, or all over) will change the results of the silver trying to emerge through the clear layer. Bursts, streaks, wisps and smooth gradients will appear in all colors of blues, greens, purples, and golden yellow.When working Amazon Night without encasement, make sure not to overwork in a reducing atmosphere or in an over oxidizing flame to avoid phase separation or scum. Work in as close to a neutral atmosphere as possible until just before putting the piece away, then increase propane in flame and pass piece through flame and watch a chrome like rainbow iridescence build up with different levels of exposure." - Mike Shelbo

40H7Et.name: Andromeda
40H7Et.description: Andromeda is a striking sparkle color that takes the Triple Passion strike and the sparkle of Paparazzi and combines them in one! Working Tip: Work this color like you would Triple Passion or a similar striking color. Since this color also has chrome it in work it in a neutral flame and garage at 975° F, Anneal at 1050° F. Artist Description by Mike Shelbo: “Andromeda is a transparent green sparkle that strikes when heated to a transparent amber that will continue to strike to a deep purple, if the layer of color is thick enough. In addition to the base color there is sparkle and silver that will fume the surface of the color as it gets worked. You can treat Andromeda similar to GA Triple Passion and use an intense, sharp flame to burn off the silver fume on the surface if you wish to show the brilliance of the sparkle in the finish of your piece. You can get a range of finishes with this color without encasement, depending on how long the color is worked and in what flame atmosphere. I have found that when encased in clear, Andromeda handles very well and the clear can often intensify the sparkle. If worked before encasement you can trap silver fuming off the color and have a milky blue ghostly veil over your sparkle green or purple. The sparkle flakes in Andromeda seem to reflect a rainbow of color, ending in gold. The color can be manipulated by twisting, compressing, layering and thinning the amount of color used and how it is worked into your piece, resulting in a number of finishing looks. When kiln striking the base color to shift into deeper colors try 1100 degrees Fahrenheit for short intervals of time until you see the desired results. Andromeda pairs well with GA Eclipse and GA Grape.” – Mike Shelbo

4b8Jbf.name: Antidote
4b8Jbf.description: This pastel green is a highly workable and compatible color. The first of our Pastel line of colors, Antidote is a tried and true green. For a darker version, check out Double Dose. Working Tip: Be sure not to get this color too hot when in a thin application as to not cook out the pastel base and turn it transparent. Work in a neutral flame. Blow outs work best with the pastel colors.

6CPj2t.name: Aquamarine
6CPj2t.description: This beautiful light blue-green is a highly usable copper free color. There is no chance of livering or REDuction with this one! If you are looking for a darker version of this color, check out Ultramarine. Working Tip: This is a user friendly color and can withstand long working times. As always, we suggest you use a neutral flame.

2Snmpe.name: Aquatic Carnival
2Snmpe.description: The color is a playful striking color, yielding creams to metallic color. It can provide very distinctive red colors when reduced.
