0AKVCH.description: Tiger's Eye is a Beryl based sparkle color utilizing the next generation sparkle technology found in Paparazzi. Working Tip: This color likes to be worked cool, but make sure you have your heat base built up while tooling or manipulating the glass to avoid developing a gray haze. Artist Description by Mike Shelbo: “I have been waiting for this sparkle for a long time. It really completes the sparkle palette for earth tones. Tiger’s Eye has such large sparkle flakes that when you catch it in different light it seems as though you see every color of the rainbow reflecting like a prism. At the same time, you can also see gold and silver flakes. The base color helps a lot with this effect. Similar to Beryl but a bit more vibrant, this transparent color works quite the same. It handles every type of working situation, although you want to avoid long exposure to a heavy propane flame. It can be worked solid or blown, thick or thin. I prefer dense layers of Tiger’s Eye so you can really see the range of spectrum within the sparkle.” – Mike Shelbo

10PbPq.name: Tonic
10PbPq.description: Tonic has a vintage glass look and is a younger sibling of Rain Drop. For best results, this crisp, high index color should be used in a neutral flame. Working Tip: Work neutral to oxidizing for best results. A reducing flame will cause red streaking. Artist Description by Mike Shelbo: "Tonic is a transparent blue, the color of an aquamarine gem. The color becomes more vibrant and its higher refractive index shows when used with itself in applications that allow the Tonic layer to be as thick as possible. When used as tubing, applied on clear or as coiled color, if the Tonic will be exposed to a lot of different working flames and long times in and out of the kiln, I advise a thin clear coat to protect the surface from overworking. Too much propane in your flame can result in a copper reduction leaving you with red streaks or patches on the surface of the un-encased Tonic. Too much over oxidizing can leave you with a surface haze or scuzz that must be swiped to remove. I often recommend a thin layer of clear frit over Tonic or evenly coated clear rod over your entire prep. I have used Tonic without encasement many times on solid sculpture and had good results, but I have seen a warming or flashing flame haze up a section. Working Tonic in as close to a neutral flame and away from the face of your torch is wise and will get you the best results with the color. If you have worked Raindrop in the past, this color is very similar in working properties. My favorite application is to gather up rods into 18mm or thicker sections and sculpt them into figurines. This next generation transparent is definitely a must have to fill out the rainbow palette. It can be layered over other colors like white for a nice pastel, but will be a faint tint unless applied as a 5-7mm thick layer. The first impression Tonic made on me was the thought that it was the color of window glass or old soda bottles, both aqua blue colors that I have always been fond of.” – Mike Shelbo

5RxVfb.name: Tree Hugger
5RxVfb.description: Tree Hugger, 4497 is darker than Shamrock and is a bold dark green. Like Shamrock, Tree Hugger is smooth, creamy and easy to work. Working Tip: Work this color in a neutral flame. Garage at 975° F, Anneal at 1050° F. Artist Description by Mike Shelbo"This opaque green is a shade darker than GA Shamrock and is equally as dense in saturation of the color. It can be drawn down to a very thin stringer and still hold its true color. It works very smooth for being such a dark green, which are often prone to stiffness. It melts easily and has no visible termination points when separated from itself. While I have had success with encasement under a thick layer of clear, I still suggest testing and experimentation when using opaque greens to check if the application works in different circumstances. GA Tree Hugger adds to the already existing ROYGBIV color fade of opaques available from GA and is becoming more and more one of my favorite colors to sculpt with. I like to pair it with GA Agua Mist.

5Wt0e3.name: Triple Passion
5Wt0e3.description: Triple Passion, 786 was introduced as an easy striking amber to purple color. Due to its formulation this color quickly, easily and consistently strikes through a wide range of bright and delightful purples. The use of color-changing borosilicate exploded soon after Glass Alchemy introduced this color to the market. This is a must have in every glass studio! Working Tip: Get this color white hot to erase the striking history. A variety of effects are achievable depending on how long you flame/kiln strike. Artist Description by Mike Shelbo: "You know it, you love it, and you can use it so many ways! Triple Passion is a striking color full of silver goodness. This means that as your translucent base glass shifts from a golden yellow to amber and into purples and violets you will also see a reaction from the silver adding in blue and green and purple hues. To best understand how this will work as you make your piece, heat your color rod to a molten state, let it cool, then with a normal working flame heat for a second at a time and pause in between to watch results. The striking happens quickly and that is why short exposure increments will yield large differences. Encase with clear to trap luster and pearlescent qualities. Color layer thickness will determine final color and ability to control finishing effects." - Mike Shelbo

1YZAr8.name: Turquoise
1YZAr8.description: Turquoise, 445 was inspired by Southwest American Indian art. To mimic natural turquoise we wanted a color that would develop organic red highlights within the green coloration like the stone. Working Tip: Work this color in a neutral flame. Garage at 975° F, Anneal at 1050° F. Use of reduction at the end of the project can produce subtle red tones. Artist Description by Mike Shelbo: "This color is a natural earth-toned opaque greenish blue. Turquoise is great for solid sculpture and blown work. The density of the color will stay true to the color of the rod before manipulation but when blown, it can become a milky translucent and opalescent version of itself. This is best achieved by sandwiching between clear and blowing thin. Turquoise works creamy but the slightest bit stiffer than other opaques. Overworking the surface of the color when not encased in clear can lead to undesired surface texture and finish. However, when desired you can use a reduction flame with heavy propane on unencased Turquoise before you put your piece in the annealer to bring out the copper, which will result in very natural toned red tints and streaks interacting with your base color." - Mike Shelbo

3z745b.name: Twilight
3z745b.description: Twilight, 548 was designed as part of a series of 6 blues and greens to provide a range of hues and intensities that would work well with each other as well as set off the bright Crayon colors. Working Tip: Work this color in a neutral flame. Garage at 975° F, Anneal at 1050° F. Artist Description by Mike Shelbo: "Twilight is the slightest bit stiffer than Glass Alchemy Peacock and Agua Azul but works just the same, nice and creamy. This blue is a deep, opaque color that is darker than Peacock, but still a very distinct blue that has a special place in the color palette. It works great for sculpting solid work and for blown work. Twilight lends well to many styles of application. I also like Twilight for murrine because of the density of the color and the ability to hold up well when drawn down to different sizes. Working this color properly is the same as working other opaques and Crayon colors. Twilight does not sublime or boil and can be intensely spot heated with a sharp flame for detail and welds. Small variations in darker tones emerge with intense spot heating when color is not encased." - Mike Shelbo

2K6CfC.name: Ultramarine
2K6CfC.description: Darker than Aquamarine, Ultramarine is a beautiful blue-green. It is a highly usable copper free color. If you like Atlantis, but are looking for a cheaper option, this is your color. There is no chance of REDuction with this one! Working Tip: This is a user friendly color and can withstand long working times. As always, we suggest you use a neutral flame.

3FhhKv.name: Unicorn Tears
3FhhKv.description: Unicorn Tears is a beautiful pink-purple with a touch of silver for a fumey effect. Working Tip: Work in a neutral flame and use a slightly reducing flame to bring the silver effects to the surface. You can also try running this color through multiple kiln cycles to activate the silver. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

1YsAZC.name: Walnut
1YsAZC.description: Walnut, 8475 was a later release. We were receiving many requests to create a color that matched the saturation of Cobalt-5, 515 in a brown tone. Recognizing that this was an important color, we did several months of development work and were very pleased to introduce Black Walnut, 8475. A deep rich opaque brown, this color works well in many applications and has become an important part of our lineup. Working Tip: Work in neutral flame to avoid reduction (gray wisps). Artist Description by Mike Shelbo: "This color is a saturated what you see is what you get opaque deep brown. It works very nicely in all flame atmospheres and in both blown and solid work. It melts into itself easily and is great for detail applied by stringers and in larger applications. Walnut seems opaque but when blown thin or applied in very thin stringers it will show its translucent quality. It can be worked for long periods of time without encasement and with heavy manipulation. This is one of the staple colors in the earth toned palette Glass Alchemy has to offer." - Mike Shelbo

6hrAu7.name: Wood Glue
6hrAu7.description: ﻿This pastel based color is back by popular demand!! Wood Glue is a sibling of Glue Stick, with a little extra something to give it a great neutral color. Working Tip: Be sure not to get this color too hot when in a thin application as to not cook out the pastel base and turn it transparent. Blow outs work best of the pastel colors. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

60eeA3.name: Yellow Crayon
60eeA3.description: Yellow Crayon is a dense, bright cadmium based school bus yellow. It is great for all applications and will remain dense when pulled down thin. Try Acid Yellow Crayon if you are looking for a little more kick in your color. Working Tip: Pre-heat in outer flame. Avoid rapid heating. Artist Description by Mike Shelbo: "This color is a true yellow opaque. It's very natural and has an earthy tone to it. Not too dark, not too bright, Yellow Crayon is just right. Works like other crayon colors and prefers to be in the mid to outer region of the flame but can come close to the torch tip in quick passes and light repeated spot heats. The color density holds well in stringers, canework, and murrine. Blowing with Yellow Crayon works well with encasement or color on the surface of your piece and will stay dense until the color layer is blown thinner than 1mm. Compliments and contrasts with almost the entire Glass Alchemy palette, try Yellow Crayon, 304 and Tiger's Eye, 8595 for bumblebees or with Shamrock, 4494 for a classic combo." - Mike Shelbo

4ZMWfh.name: Zen
4ZMWfh.description: Zen is a beautiful soft aqua blue-green that adds a tranquil touch to the pastel line-up. Zen is a pastel version of Tonic, and does contain copper. For a copper free version, try Nimbus. Working Tip: Work neutral to oxidizing for best results. A reducing flame will cause REDuction. While this color can be worked without encasement, for longer working times, we recommend a thin sleeve of clear. Be sure not to get this color too hot when in a thin application as to not cook out the pastel base and turn it transparent. Blow outs work best of the pastel colors.

5K0JuV.name: Acadian Night (Dense Silver)
5K0JuV.description: Acadian Night is a dense sparkle color with a blue hue and silver striking effect.

1nKn5M.name: Acadian Night
1nKn5M.description: Our newest batch of Acadian Night is a sparkle color with a blue hue and silver striking effect.

3G1VSY.name: Autumn Sample Packs
3G1VSY.description: The seasons are changing and we have a sample pack to match. These are a mix of B/B+ quality, weigh 1lb 1oz and come with two rods of each color. Dense Pineapple Juice, Mango, Exp. Green Olive, Russet, Transitional Cinnabar, and Moist Raspberry.

1xcgFw.name: Blue Cheese
1xcgFw.description: A true staple of the Greasy collection, Blue Cheese is a Creamy opaque blue that really pops.

5NGpfX.name: Blue Satin
5NGpfX.description: One of our classic colors. A royal blue color with a satin sheen.

3vL1eK.name: Chocolate Opal (Dense)
3vL1eK.description: A dense version of our Chocolate Opal, this color looks purple or brown in different lights.

3Z6P0t.name: Chocolate Opal
3Z6P0t.description: Chocolate Opal features many vibrant hues that shift in different light spectrums, from deep purple to brilliant brown.

1NCbGa.name: Creme Brulee
1NCbGa.description: A Creamy color that can be used in multiple applications.

5Ebj6R.name: Dark Wildberry Satin
5Ebj6R.description: Darker variety of Wildberry with satin chatoyancy. This shade is nice and dark when solid, and can be sleeved or thinned for a more transparent or translucent finish.

3FYD63.name: Dense Glopal
3FYD63.description: This is a odd batch of dense Glopal rod with a slight satin.

5u54xC.name: Dense Orange Opal (Unique)
5u54xC.description: This is a dense opal orange color with slight satin. Best worked in a gentle flame or encased.

0wuaV0.name: Dense Pineapple Juice
0wuaV0.description: This is a lovely dense cadmium yellow based color.

4Qt9s8.name: Dense Rose Quartz
4Qt9s8.description: Dense Rose Quartz is a dense version Rose Quartz with extra milky opal effect. Under CFL it goes to a more intense electric hot pink.

0KCq6S.name: Diet Blue Cheese (Variant)
0KCq6S.description: This is a variant of our diet blue cheese. A lighter version of our classic blue cheese.

0wHNjp.name: Euro
0wHNjp.description: A clear that glows blue under UV.

6ghkh2.name: Exp. Black Pearl
6ghkh2.description: Experience the beauty of the Exp. Black Pearl Rod - a stunning, rod with an opalescent finish and a satin feel. Slowly pre heat rod and work it gently.

3zmm0g.name: Exp. Black
3zmm0g.description: Greasy Glass black rod. Our black consists of a super dense Wildberry variable. When thinned or exposed to bright backlight the color can show blue/purple. Keep dense for the most black affect.

2xpM5w.name: Exp. Blood Orange
2xpM5w.description: Vibrant transparent orange. There are some subtle variations in the strike from yellow to red and orange.

3RdpQC.name: Exp. Blood Red
3RdpQC.description: Bright yet deep toned transparent red rod that really pops.

6zkugt.name: Exp. Blood Red (unique)
6zkugt.description: Bright yet deep transparent red rod that really pops. This unique batch varies slightly in tone from the original, almost in the direction of a red orange though still definitely in the Blood Red family.

4CRd5e.name: Exp. Blue Phoenix
4CRd5e.description: A blue striking opal color that produces a range of hues from red to purple.

0GZQEv.name: Exp. Blueberry Opal
0GZQEv.description: This is a navy blue color in the same family as sonic.

63Ldhe.name: Exp. Bronze Pearl
63Ldhe.description: A Stunning experimental bronze colored extremely metallic looking color with opalescence to rival a pearl. Bronze Pearl shimmers and shines like a brilliant sparkle color, and also contains depth from the opal effect. This unique batch may have variations in color, and crystal size.

14taHN.name: Exp. Cinnabar
14taHN.description: A dense orange cadmium based color.

3Ps0Zd.name: Exp. Coral
3Ps0Zd.description: This is a cadmium based orange that looks similar to the marine invertebrates at the bottom of the sea.

2gRTkz.name: Exp. Coraline Satin
2gRTkz.description: Coraline Satin is a cadmium red satin color worked best in a gentle flame or encased. This is a limited batch available while supplies last.

2FAQgR.name: Exp. Cosmos
2FAQgR.description: A silver striking black that produces a range of colors.

5sjQfc.name: Exp. Dark Blue Raspberry
5sjQfc.description: Intriguing dark striking rod combining a medium saturation cobalt blue and a strong transparent ruby that strikes in the flame as well as the kiln.

5vGC5A.name: Exp. Dark Green Pearl
5vGC5A.description: Similar to Bronze Pearl, this Experimental Dark Green version appears dark and mysterious.

2xZC0w.name: Exp. Dense Coral (variant)
2xZC0w.description: This is similar to our coral but a little bit more opaque. Best worked in a gentle flame or encased.

3rKVGH.name: Exp. Dense Yellow Opal
3rKVGH.description: This is a vivid yellow with opal qualities. Color works best in a neutral to oxidizing flame or encased.

6F8sLt.name: Exp. Dense Yellow Opal (unique)
6F8sLt.description: This Exp. Dense Yellow Opal Rod is an ideal choice for a one-of-a-kind piece. Its unique mustard color and dense opal structure provide a visually striking effect.

4vjLAK.name: Exp. Desert Rose
4vjLAK.description: This is a cadmium-based orange with pinkish blush tones. Works best in a gentle flame or encased.

09cRCZ.name: Exp. Poofs (Dense)
09cRCZ.description: A cadmium based orange works best in neutral flame.

3bGNRr.name: Exp. Green Olive
3bGNRr.description: This is an experimental green color, best worked gently in neutral to oxidizing flames or encased.

6Axj1t.name: Exp. Green Opal (Dense)
6Axj1t.description: This is a one of our new green opal colors, this is a dense batch.

40Z641.name: Exp. Green Opal (unique)
40Z641.description: A cadmium based green opal. This color works best in neutral to oxidizing flames or encased. This batch is slightly different than the original.

3q6bP7.name: Exp. Green Opal
3q6bP7.description: A cadmium based green opal. This color works best in neutral to oxidizing flames or encased.

318sJ9.name: Exp. Light Blue Crimson
318sJ9.description: Exp. Light Blue Crimson is a flame striking red with a light blue cobalt base.

2dYUPr.name: Exp. Light Orange Rainbow
2dYUPr.description: This color can produce a range of colors. Samples were struck in the kiln at 1125 for a short amount of time.

0x9yPP.name: Exp. Orange
0x9yPP.description: A vivid semi transparent cadmium based orange.

3pS5TR.name: Exp. Pink Grapefruit
3pS5TR.description: This is an experimental orange/pink cadmium color with similarities to orange opal.

4LJdJ6.name: Exp. Sonic Satin (Dense)
4LJdJ6.description: Our classic sonic with a satin twist.

4pE8Nn.name: Exp. Transparent Green
4pE8Nn.description: An experimental transparent green. Best worked in an oxidizing flame or encased.

59G52V.name: Exp. Yellow Opal
59G52V.description: Our newest batch of yellow opal rod. A vivid cadmium yellow with opal qualities best worked in a soft flame or encased.

37PKtJ.name: Globalt
37PKtJ.description: Global is a light cobalt color that glows a strong blue under UV light.

3bWkCN.name: Glopal
3bWkCN.description: Glopal is an easy to work and stable opal with a pink UV glow. Milky opaque appearance to unworked tube, with UV glow and opal quality allowing for more or less transparency depending on working conditions. Use a hotter flame for more transparent finish and less heat for a more opaque final product. A thin layer of clear adds durability for higher temp flames and sculpting.

3g3V97.name: Gold Purple
3g3V97.description: A gold based purple opal color. Color needs to be full worked for purple to strike. To avoid hazing on gold colors work in neutral to oxidizing flame or encase.

520eDM.name: Grease Stain (Light Strike)
520eDM.description: A yellowish color with light silver striking characteristics.

3YXQaC.name: Green Energy (Light Strike)
3YXQaC.description: This is a silver striking green, you can get a range of color from due to the striking properties.

1TmHHA.name: Ice Water (UV)
1TmHHA.description: This icy looking transparent glows pink under blacklight. A subtle hint of satin creates the ice water effect, resulting in a standalone clear transparent, or as a component in building layered colored tubes.

6CUBD6.name: Icy Blue Satin
6CUBD6.description: A icy blue with a satin shimmer and Uv reactive.

5gW0xF.name: Jungle Juice (variant)
5gW0xF.description: Jungle Juice is a rich dark green color with sparkle effect. Work gently and does not like deep encasements.

1RFP2c.name: Light Bright
1RFP2c.description: A clear that glows Pink/Orange under Uv light.

2p5yRb.name: Light Olive Oil
2p5yRb.description: A transparent yellow with slight opal affect.

2X639Z.name: Light Phoenix
2X639Z.description: Light Phoenix appears as a bright and rich ruby red. Very similar shade of red as standard Phoenix with a finished appearance closer to a traditional ruby red than an opal version. This is a perfect option when seeking a true transparent red that shines bright. Light Phoenix may appear transparent clear when working and before annealing. For a faster strike, raise kiln temperature as high as 1100.

3k1A0Y.name: Light Russet
3k1A0Y.description: A light brown with a slit tint of orange.

19Puyt.name: Mango
19Puyt.description: Mango is a vibrant translucent yellow orange in the pineapple juice family. Best worked in a gentle flame or encased.

12NxRm.name: Marina (Dense)
12NxRm.description: A denser batch than our classic Marina. Works best in neutral to oxidizing flames or encased.

3G6XPX.name: Marina
3G6XPX.description: Crisp aquatic blue reminiscent of a clear pond on a bright summer day, Marina is a copper based opal blue. Marina is similar to and in the family of Hydro. Like all opal type colors, it will appear more transparent when worked hotter and more milky when worked cooler. This new batch is slightly more transparent than the last batch.

0nWhjD.name: Moist Raspberry (Unique)
0nWhjD.description: This Moist Raspberry (Unique) Rod adds a vibrant pop of color to any project with its flame striking ruby red hue.

1tUe3p.name: Moist Raspberry
1tUe3p.description: A striking red, for best results flame strike then kiln strike.

5dkxbZ.name: Neo Opal (Dense)
5dkxbZ.description: A more dense version of our classic Neo Opal.

3AtgRA.name: Neo Opal
3AtgRA.description: Our classic Neo Opal Rod a translucent purple color with opal properties.

0ECFWx.name: Opal Light
0ECFWx.description: Opal Light is a lighter variety of Gopal with the same working characteristics. It has less opal strike which makes this a good color for overlay variations.

5RQyPL.name: Peach Opal Agate
5RQyPL.description: Lovely pinkish opal color that verges into an occasional amber.

1RT7Qm.name: Phoenix
1RT7Qm.description: Phoenix is juicy opal red color in the range of ruby with flashes of purple. Phoenix can produce a range of colors depending on strike.

5hBWvB.name: Pineapple
5hBWvB.description: Pineapple is a light yellow cadmium color worked best in a gentle neutral flame.

6a9BP4.name: Pumpkin
6a9BP4.description: A cadmium based color in similar shade to that of a pumpkin.

3YUQLQ.name: Purple Rainbow (unique)
3YUQLQ.description: A unique Striking purple rainbow. Wonderful silver based striking effect in this transparent purple. Work this color using flame chemistry in between neutral and oxidizing to maintain transparency. Strike using a slightly reducing flame or by leaving to soak in the kiln. Note that raising the temperature of the kiln is not always necessary for striking purple rainbow. 1080F for 3 - 4 hours

495Mqg.name: Rainbow Opal
495Mqg.description: The Rainbow Opal Rod adds a unique level of color and shimmer in the flame with its opalescent rainbow color shift. It works in both oxidizing and neutral atmospheres and contains a combination of opal and cfl to maximize color enhancement. Its striking effects add a vibrant decorative touch to any glass design.

3PsRsS.name: Rainbow Sample Pack V12
3PsRsS.description: These rainbow sample packs are darker/dense opal colors. They contain two rods of each color, Dark Phoenix, Russet Opal, Yellow Opal Satin, Green Opal, Blueberry Opal, and Dense Neo Opal.

6gBuFx.name: Rainbow Sample Pack V13
6gBuFx.description: These rainbow sample packs have 2 rods of each of the following colors Dark Phoenix, Exp. Orange, Dense Yellow Opal, Green Opal, Sonic, and Dense Neo Opal.

4LpgJW.name: Rainbow Sample Pack V14

6FyxEp.name: Oracle-754.opl
6FyxEp.description: Summary: Slow Opal. Description: 754.opl is a slow opal that strikes in the flame and kiln. When reset it is crystal clear and when fully struck it’s milky opaque white. Areas that have started to opacify in the flame will continue to opacify in the annealer. Striking temperatures are lower than that of our silver glasses. Working notes: This slow opal stays mostly reset during many beadmaking operations, and will strike to a misty-opal during annealing. I anneal this color at 975°F for up to five hours for misty-opal beads, depending on size, encasement, and other factors. Your kiln is probably different than mine. Test beads are recommended. -Jed at Double Helix Glassworks

6gwAKP.name: Helios
6gwAKP.description: Summary: Reduction Color. Description: Helios is a golden-yellow silver-reduction glass that develops a metallic luster when reduced. Pink-tinged highlights develop with repeated reduction. Helios works best in surface applications. Work in a neutral flame. Cool until the glass is no longer glowing. Expose the glass to a reduction flame, while keeping it from getting hot. Brief (5-10 seconds) and repeated exposures produces the best results. See our How To section for more detailed working information and tips on using our reduction colors.

6v3aHY.name: Oracle-754.opl
6v3aHY.description: Summary: Slow Opal. Description: 754.opl is a slow opal that strikes in the flame and kiln. When reset it is crystal clear and when fully struck it’s milky opaque white. Areas that have started to opacify in the flame will continue to opacify in the annealer. Striking temperatures are lower than that of our silver glasses. Working notes: This slow opal stays mostly reset during many beadmaking operations, and will strike to a misty-opal during annealing. I anneal this color at 975°F for up to five hours for misty-opal beads, depending on size, encasement, and other factors. Your kiln is probably different than mine. Test beads are recommended. -Jed at Double Helix Glassworks

5bfCeu.name: Aquatic Carnival

5DXDV6.name: Transparent Shifty Peach Opal
5DXDV6.description: A transparent version of our shifty peach. Changes from peach to bright pink under cfl light.

305yrr.name: Transparent Shifty Sauce

2m5kDU.description: A yellow with light opal, use neutral flame for best results.

0eEa64.name: Yoshi

3wzvS1.name: Clear

6H4HZz.name: Cotton Candy
6H4HZz.description: Cotton Candy is a CFL shifter on a pastel base. This color is creamy and easy to work. Violet under natural light, the color will shift to a soft blue under CFL. Working Tip: Be sure not to get this color too hot when in a thin application as to not cook out the pastel base and turn it transparent. Work in a neutral flame. Blow outs work best with the pastel colors. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

4KW0X8.name: Double Dragon Hoodie
4KW0X8.description: A soft and comfy unisex hoodie that fits all your hoodie needs. The Bella + Canvas fleece fabric makes it a great partner all year round. • 52% airlume combed and ring-spun cotton, 48% poly fleece* • Hood • Side seamed • Retail fit *Heather Colors: 60% airlume combed and ring-spun cotton, 40% poly fleece The male model is wearing size M. He's 6.0 feet (183 cm) tall, chest circumference 42.5" (108 cm), waist circumference 33.5" (85 cm). The female model is wearing a size M. She's 5.8 feet (178 cm) tall, chest circumference 34.6" (88 cm), waist circumference 27.1" (69 cm) and hip circumference 37.7" (96 cm). * Merch orders ship separately.

5hp7XN.name: Dragon Tears
5hp7XN.description: Dragon Tears is a transparent blue silver. This color is playful, while remaining transparent once worked. Working Tip: Work in a neutral flame and use a slightly reducing flame to bring the silver effects to the surface. Long kiln times will darken the effects, the base color will stay the same. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.

You can also try running this color through multiple kiln cycles to activate the silver. Note: Thomas' Test Lab contains good quality glass. The color formulation is still not final and final QC parameters have not been set.
